body:
다음 대화의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을모두 골라 짝지은 것은?

G: Hey, did you watch the nature documentary the
teacher recommended?
B:
You mean the ⓐone about the endangered
species around us? No, I didn’t. Was it good?
G: Yes, it was. I was particularly impressed by the
part about the Eurasian otters.
B: Oh, you mean the long, thin creatures ⓑthat
like water? I heard they are very intelligent,
playful, and excellent at catching fish.
G: They ⓒsure are. They can swim at the speed of
12 kilometers per hour and dive as ⓓdeep as
14 meters.
B: That’s cool. But why are they endangered?
G: In the past, they were hunted for their expensive
fur and skin. Nowadays, the bigger threat is the
loss of their habitats due to human activities.
B: ⓔHow a shame! Shouldn’t we do something
about it?
G: Fortunately, thanks to conservation efforts, their
population is now recovering and more and
more are ⓕspotting around us.
B: Oh, that’s a relief.
solution: ⓔ How → What (뒤에 관사 a와 명사 shame이 이어지므로, ‘What+a(n)(+형용사)+명사(구)(+주어+동사)!’ 형태의 감탄문이 되도록 How를 What으로 고친다. 참고로, How가 이끄는 감탄 문은 ‘How+형용사/부사(+주어+동사)’의 구조로 나타낸다.) ⓕ spotting → being spotted (등위접속사 and로 연결되는 절 에 앞의 절(their population is now recovering)과 마찬가지로 현재 진행 중인 일을 나타내는 현재진행형(be동사+현재분사) 이 쓰이는 것은 알맞으나, 주어인 more and more(점점 더 많 은 것들)가 ‘발견되는’ 대상이며 뒤에 목적어 없이 부사구 around us만 이어지고 있으므로, 앞의 be동사 are와 함께 현 재진행 수동태(be동사+being+p.p.)를 이루도록 being spotted 로 고친다.)

body:
Jo: Your new book says ⓐwhat every spring and fall,
hundreds of millions to billions of migratory birds
pass over our roofs, but we seem to have no
idea that it’s ⓑhappening. Why is that?
Weidensaul: Well, most birds migrate after dark,
including almost all of the birds that ⓒis
normally active during the day. (A)그것이 우리가
이동이 일어나고 있다는 걸 알아차리기 어려운 이유
이다. They migrate at night because the night sky
is cooler, and ⓓthe air calmer. Besides, there are
fewer ⓔpredators at night. If you ⓕcan strip
away the night sky and make everything visible,
this migration would probably be the largest,
greatest natural spectacle on the planet.
Jo: Among those global travelers in your book, I
found the bar-tailed godwits to be particularly
impressive.
Weidensaul: Sure. Some of them can even make a
10,000 km non-stop journey across the Pacific
Ocean, from western Alaska to New Zealand in
11 days.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

Weidensaul: Birds in migratory condition can do
things that they can’t do at other times of the
year. Another neat trick you might envy is that
they can gain a tremendous amount of muscle
tissue without exercise. For example, before
some
bar-tailed
godwits

Alaska

_________. They just eat and eat until they
double their weight. By the time they take off,
their
heart
and
flight
muscles
may
have
increased by 50%. After they have eaten as
much as they possibly can and can’t put any
more weight on, their digestive organs shrink
dramatically because these won’t be put to use

choices: rigid dieting
binge feeding
physical training
muscle reduction
excessive hydration천재(강상구) 4과

body:
Jo: How do they travel such a long distance over a
nearly featureless ocean?
Weidensaul: To find their routes, the bar-tailed
godwits probably rely on the sun and stars
among other things. Some experts believe that
they may be able to sense the earth’s magnetic
field lines, too. You may also wonder how, if
ever, they sleep while flying over a vast ocean.
(A)철새들은 ‘반뇌수면’이라고 불리는 방법을 사용
하는 것으로 밝혀집니다. This is how it works.
Only the left half of the brain sleeps for a
couple of seconds, then only the right half for
the next couple of seconds, and then this
process repeats over and over again. Isn’t it
amazing? Actually, some sea mammals like
dolphins can do that, too, because they have
to keep breathing consciously.
Jo: That’s a neat trick. Who wouldn’t like to have
such an ability?

다음 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?

Weidensaul: Birds in migratory condition can do
things that they can’t do at other times of the
year.
(A) After they have eaten as much as they possibly
can and can’t put any more weight on, their
digestive organs shrink dramatically because
these won’t be put to use during the non-stop
flight to New Zealand.
(B) Another neat trick you might envy is that they
can gain a tremendous amount of muscle tissue
without exercise. For example, before some
bar-tailed godwits leave Alaska in September
and make a 10,000 km flight across the Pacific,
they undergo a process of binge feeding.
(C) They just eat and eat until they double their
weight. By the time they take off, their heart
and flight muscles may have increased by 50%.
solution: 이동을 하는 상태의 새들은 연중 다른 시기에는 할 수 없는 일 들을 해낼 수 있다는 내용의 주어진 글에 이어, 그중 하나인 신 기한 재주로서 ‘이동을 하는 상태의 새들’을 they로 받아, 그들이 운동을 하지 않고도 엄청난 양의 근육 조직을 만들 수 있다는 내용과, 이에 대한 예시로서 어떤 큰뒷부리도요가 9월에 알래스 카를 떠나 태평양을 가로질러 1만 킬로미터를 날기 전에 폭식의 과정을 거친다는 (B), ‘어떤 큰뒷부리도요들’을 They로 받아 그들 이 몸무게가 두 배가 될 때까지 계속 먹는다는 내용과, 출발할 때쯤 그들의 심장과 비상근이 50% 정도 늘어나게 된다는 (C), 이 새들이 이동을 시작한 이후에 일어나는 일로서, 그들이 먹을 수 있는 한 많이 먹어서 더 이상 몸무게가 늘지 않으면 소화 기 관들이 급격히 위축되는데, 뉴질랜드까지 계속 나는 동안에는 이것들이 사용되지 않기 때문이라는 (A)의 흐름이 자연스럽다. 천재(강상구) 4과

body:
Today, I’m looking for a tiny animal that’s hiding
in one of Europe’s most beautiful capital cities,
Vienna. Now it’s home to nearly 2 million people,
but 50% of the city is green space. What I’m
looking for is probably one of Europe’s most
critically endangered mammals.
Now, I’ve come really early to a graveyard to try to
see some hamsters because this is one of the best
times of day to see them. At this time of the day,
there’s nobody around so they don’t have to avoid
people while (A)[looked / looking] for food. These
little ones have been in the area for decades, but
now live among the dead because development has
robbed them of the green fields they used to inhabit.
Look! I just found one over there. See how (B)[is
it / it is] trying to stuff its cheeks full? Hamsters
can pack a quarter of their body weight inside their
cheeks, which helps them (C)[get / getting] through
the winter. Surprisingly, they not only feed on nuts
and flowers, but have also adapted to eating candle
wax, which is a good source of fat and is easy to
find in graveyards.
Even though the hamsters here have adapted to
the noises of the city, they still keep a watchful
eye, as predators are never too far away. They may
need to quickly escape back down into their holes,
which are complex structures stretching under the
ground. Despite urban areas generally having a
negative effect on wildlife, cities can actually provide
islands of protection for it.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)          (B)          (C)
choices: lookingis itget
lookedit isget
lookedis itgetting
lookingit isget
lookingit isgetting
solution: (A) 부사절 접속사 while 뒤에 주어와 동사가 있는 완전한 절이 와야 하나 뒤에 다른 동사(구)가 없으므로 주어를 이끄는 동명사 가 쓰일 수 없고, 주어 없이 동사구를 이룰 수도 없으므로, 접속 사를 남겨둔 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이다. 주절 주어와 동일 한 분사구문의 의미상 주어 they가 some hamsters(어떤 햄스터 들)를 가리키며, ‘찾는’ 주체이고, ‘look for ~(~을 찾다)’의 look은 자동사이므로, 능동의 의미를 지닌 현재분사 looking이 알맞다. (B) how 이하는 동사 See의 목적어로 쓰인 간접의문문이므로 의문 부사 how 뒤에 ‘주어+동사’의 평서문 어순을 이루는 it is가 알맞다. (C) 동사 helps와 목적어인 대명사 them에 이어져 ‘help+목적 어+목적격보어’(~가 …하도록 돕다)의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목 적격보어 자리로, help는 목적격보어로 동사원형이나 to부정사 를 취하는 동사이므로 동사원형 get이 알맞다.

body:
Jo: Then what happens after they arrive there?
Weidensaul: They regrow their digestive organs and
spend the summer (A)[feed / feeding] again,
and they undergo the same journey back to
Alaska. They do this again and again for 25 to
30 years, flying up to 30,000 km every year. By
the time bar-tailed godwits die, they have flown
close to twice the distance from Earth to the moon.
Jo: That’s truly impressive. By the way, I hear you’ve
visited Korea several times before. Why do you
come here so often?
Weidensaul: As a bird watcher and conservationist, I
find the Yellow Sea mudflats between Korea and
China very special. They are some of the largest
tidal mudflats on the earth and (B)[provide /
providing] a critical stopover point for the
countless
migratory
birds
on
the
East
Asian-Australasian Flyway. While these enormous
stretches of tidal mud look featureless to the
human eye, they ⓐ________________________________.
Jo: So the mudflats are drawing all kinds of birds in
from as far away as New Zealand, Australia, and Asia?
Weidensaul: Yes. Many of these birds fly several
thousand kilometers to get to the Yellow Sea.
Here, they have to double their weight in less
than two weeks and make another flight of
several thousand kilometers up north. That’s why
the Yellow Sea is so critically important. It’s one
of the few places in the world where migratory
birds can get the resources (C)[that / what] they
need on their difficult journey.
*East Asian-Australasian Flyway: 동아시아-대양주 철새 이동 경로

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)            (B)           (C)
choices: feedprovidethat
feedingprovidingthat
feedingprovidewhat
feedingprovidethat
feedprovidingwhat
solution: (A) 동사 spend와 시간 명사구 the summer에 이어지고 있으므 로, ‘~하면서 (시간)을 보내다’라는 뜻의 ‘spend+시간+-ing’ 구 문을 이루는 -ing 형태의 feeding이 알맞다. (B) 주어 They에 이어지는 복수동사 are와 등위접속사 and로 병렬연결을 이루어야 하며, 뒤에 목적어인 a critical stopover point가 이어지므로 능동태 복수동사인 provide가 알맞다. (C) 타동사 need의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(they ~ journey)을 이끌어 선행사인 the resources를 수식하는 관계사 절을 이루어야 하므로, 목적격 관계대명사 that이 알맞다. 참고 로, 관계대명사 what은 선행사를 포함해 ‘~한 것(들)’이라는 뜻 으로 불완전한 절을 이끈다.

into

up

Paintings of Rob Gonsalves, a Canadian magic
realist artist, ⓐcombine two different points of view.
(A)They give the viewer the visual illusion that
(B)they are looking at two unrelated realities
flawlessly ⓑfuse in one painting. They usually depict
landscapes and objects that seem to change from
one thing to another.
When you look at the top right corner of the
painting above, you can see a kid ⓒjumping on his
bed. However, as you move your eyes across, the
bedcovers change into fields, which a girl now
appears to be flying over. This is how the visual
illusion is created: an object is gradually changed
through a series of similar shapes into something
entirely ⓓdifferent in a single scene. At the same
time, two different parts of the same scene are
constructed at different scales. The result is an
unexpected and seemingly impossible whole.
This kind of illusion has a fun way of twisting your
perception. It makes you ⓔto question what is real.
Most of his incredible paintings have an unclear
boundary between the multiple stories (C)they tell,
which forces the viewer to jump back and forth
between (D)them. Tracing the transitions, you get
that delightful “Ah-ha!” feeling as you try to decide
exactly where one world transforms into another.

Fun Shadows
When we look at shadows of objects in real life,
most of us think nothing of them. Belgian artist
and film-maker Vincent Bal, however, turns them
into art forms. He lets his creativity ⓐto flow to
make beautiful and meaningful scenes with shadows.
His playful shadow art illustrations are made ㉠____
__________________________________________________________,
like a flower or a glass. In one image, the shadow
from a key is reinterpreted as a DJ ⓑwearing
headphones. In another, a potato peeler creates the
perfectly shaped frame for a piano. In his art, the
shadow from a glass becomes a pool.
He uses a very simple process to draw his
pictures. To start the process, all he needs to do is
ⓒprepare a plain object, a piece of paper, and a
light. Then he puts the object on the paper and
turns on the light. He just starts moving the light
around and places the object in different positions.
He keeps a very open mind and tries not to have
an idea in advance about what the result should
be.
“If I try to shape a shadow into a certain form, it
always feels a bit forced. If nothing comes, I take
another object, and then I just start playing around
with it until suddenly I see something. In this way, I
can create whatever I want,” he says. His free
artistic interpretation of shadows means that the
possibilities for creating new doodles are endless.
In fact, ㉡그가 예술 작품을 만들기 시작한 것은 우
연한 일이었다. While he was working on a new
script, he suddenly noticed how the shadow of a
cup on his desk looked like a little elephant. He
completed the image with a few lines, took a
picture and shared it on the Internet. The reactions
were so positive ⓓwhat he challenged himself to
make one shadow image every day.
Art can inspire you to see the world from a new
angle. ⓔConnecting ideas that at first glance
appear unrelated is a powerful tool for exploring
the beauty of the world around us. To make such
connections, all you need is your imaginative power.

윗글의 빈칸 ㉠에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: by depicting a certain scene from fairy taleswith shadows
by strictly controlling shadows to shape theminto a fixed form
by drawing a series of changes in shadows toform a certain shape
by adding his own doodles to shadows castfrom everyday objects
by overlaying digital illustrations onto thepictures of common objects
solution: 정답은 ④ 이다. (해설 없음)

body:
I became a book artist almost by accident. After
graduating in 2003, I traveled to Thailand. At that
time, I didn’t think about working with books.
Shopping in Bangkok, I came across a used book
with beautiful notes written in it. That got me
interested in the way paper was used in art. Soon
after I returned to the UK, my father passed away.
Feeling sad, I found myself picking up the Graham
Greene classic I had brought back from my trip and
___________________________________________. I then hung
them over the open book. Since then, I have
created sculptures out of books.
I always read the story first to get inspiration, and
everything for the sculpture is made from the
pages
within
that
book;
some
don’t
have
illustrations, so I take inspiration from the title and
the text. I am also drawn toward fairy tales,
especially Hans Christian Andersen’s; his tales are
quite magical, but there’s also a sadness as they
don’t always have a happy ending.
For me, books are not only sources of ideas and
associations, but also objects of great beauty to be
cut up and rearranged. I use very simple tools: a
sharp knife, a bit of glue, and some wire. Utilizing
the open book as my base, I cut its pages, glue
them, gently pull them up, and support them with
wire. Through these processes, I construct physical
representations of the narratives and the characters.

choices: writing a letter to my father
sketching scenes on the pages
finishing a whole book in one sitting
cutting paper moths out of the pages
adding some illustrations on each page
solution: 정답은 ④ 이다. (해설 없음)

Jo: Your new book says every spring and fall,
hundreds of millions to billions of migratory
birds pass over our roofs, but we seem to have
no idea ⓐthat it’s happening. Why is that?

ⓑincluding almost all of the birds that are
normally active during the day. That’s ⓒwhy
it’s hard for us to realize the migration is
happening. They migrate at night because the
night sky is cooler, and ⓓthe air calmer. Besides,
there are fewer predators at night. If you could
strip away the night sky and make everything
visible, this migration would probably be the
largest, greatest natural spectacle on the planet.

found the bar-tailed godwits ⓔto be particularly
impressive.

10,000 km non-stop journey across the Pacific
Ocean, from western Alaska to New Zealand in
11 days.

Jo: Your new book says every spring and fall,
hundreds of millions to billions of migratory
birds pass over our roofs, but we seem to have
no idea ⓐthat it’s happening. Why is that?
Weidensaul: Well, most birds migrate after dark,
ⓑincluding almost all of the birds that are
normally active during the day. That’s ⓒwhy
it’s hard for us to realize the migration is
happening. They migrate at night because the
night sky is cooler, and ⓓthe air calmer. Besides,
there are fewer predators at night. If you could
strip away the night sky and make everything
visible, this migration would probably be the
largest, greatest natural spectacle on the planet.
Jo: Among those global travelers in your book, I
found the bar-tailed godwits ⓔto be particularly
impressive.
Weidensaul: Sure. Some of them can even make a
10,000 km non-stop journey across the Pacific
Ocean, from western Alaska to New Zealand in
11 days.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

Jo: Hello, listeners. Did you know (A)[that / what]
there are times at night when a massive
migration happens right over your heads? The
scale of migration involving billions of birds
traveling up to thousands of kilometers (B)[leave
/ leaves] you in awe. On today’s Jo’s Tea Time,
we invite naturalist and author Scott Weidensaul
to share his knowledge. He’s spent decades
(C)[to study / studying] migratory birds, writing
about them, and engaging in conservation
efforts. Welcome to the show, Mr. Weidensaul.
Weidensaul: Thanks for having me, Jo.
(A)           (B)             (C)
choices: thatleavestudying
whatleavesstudying
whatleaveto study
thatleavesstudying
thatleavesto study
solution: (A) 동사 know의 목적어 자리에서 완전한 절(there ~ heads) 을 이끌고 있으므로, 명사절 접속사인 that이 알맞다. 참고로, 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 또는 의문대명사 what은 불완 전한 절을 이끌어 문장에서 주어, 목적어, 보어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이룬다. (B) 주어부 ‘The scale of migration ~ kilometers’에 이어진 문 장의 동사 자리로, 주어부의 핵심 단어인 scale이 단수명사이 므로, 이에 수일치된 단수동사 leaves가 알맞다. (C) 과거분사 spent와 시간 명사 decades에 이어지고 있으며, 뒤에 writing, engaging이 ‘A, B, and C’의 구조로 병렬연결을 이루므로, ‘~하면서 (시간)을 보내다’라는 뜻의 ‘spend+시간 +-ing’ 구문을 이루는 -ing 형태의 studying이 알맞다. 천재(강상구) 4과

body:
Weidensaul: Birds in migratory condition can do   ⓐ
things that they can’t do at other times of the
year. (A)여러분이 부러워할지도 모르는 또 다른 신기
한 재주는 그들이 운동 없이 엄청난 양의 근육 조직
을 얻을 수 있다는 것입니다. For example, before
some bar-tailed godwits leave Alaska in September
and make a 10,000 km flight across the Pacific,
they undergo a process of binge feeding. They just
eat and eat until they double their weight. ⓑBy
the time they take off, their heart and flight
muscles may have increased by 50%. After ⓒthey
have eaten as much as they possibly can and can’t
put any more weight on, their digestive organs
shrink dramatically because these won’t be put to
use during the non-stop flight to New Zealand.
Jo: Then what happens after they arrive there?
Weidensaul: They regrow their digestive organs and
spend the summer feeding again, and they
undergo the same journey back to Alaska. They
do this again and again for 25 to 30 years,
ⓓflying up to 30,000 km every year. By the time
bar-tailed godwits die, they have flown close to
twice the distance from Earth to the moon.
Jo: That’s truly impressive. By the way, ⓔI hear
you’ve visited Korea several times before. Why
do you come here so often?

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ를 아래와 같이 전환할 때, 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: what they can’t do
ⓑ: By the time which they take off
ⓒ: they have eaten as much as possible
ⓓ: as they fly up to 30,000 km every year
ⓔ: I hear that you’ve visited Korea several times before
solution: ⓑ By the time 뒤에 ‘자동사+부사’ 구조의 take off가 쓰인 완 전한 절(they take off)이 이어져 있으므로, the time 뒤에 시간 의 관계부사 when이나 관계부사 대용의 that, 또는 선행사에 어울리는 전치사를 쓴 ‘전치사+관계대명사’인 at which가 생략 된 것으로 볼 수 있다. 따라서 By the time 뒤에 which가 아니 라 when, that, 또는 at which를 사용해 ‘By the time when[that/at which] they take off로 전환해야 한다.

Today, I’m looking for a tiny animal that’s hiding
in one of Europe’s most beautiful capital cities,
Vienna. Now it’s home to nearly 2 million people,
but 50% of the city is green space. What I’m
looking for is probably one of Europe’s most
critically endangered mammals.
Now, I’ve come really early to a graveyard to try
to see some hamsters because this is one of the
best times of day to see them. At this time of the
day, there’s nobody around so they don’t have to
avoid people while looking for food. These little
ones have been in the area for decades, but now
live among the dead because (A)개발이 그들에게서
그들이 살던 푸른 들판들을 앗아갔다.
Look! I just found one over there. See how it is
trying to stuff its cheeks full? Hamsters can pack a
quarter of their body weight inside their cheeks,
which
helps
them
get
through
the
winter.
Surprisingly, they not only feed on nuts and
flowers, but have also adapted to eating candle
wax, which is a good source of fat and is easy to
find in graveyards.
Even though the hamsters here have adapted to
the noises of the city, they still keep a watchful
eye, as predators are never too far away. They may
need to quickly escape back down into their holes,
which are complex structures stretching under the
ground. Despite urban areas generally having a

Jo: How do they travel ⓐa such long distance over
a nearly (A)featureless ocean?
Weidensaul: ⓑTo find their routes, the bar-tailed
godwits probably rely on the sun and stars
among other things. Some experts believe
ⓒthat they may be able to (B)sense the earth’s
magnetic field lines, too. You may also wonder
how, if ever, they sleep while ⓓflying over a
vast ocean. ⓔIt turns out that migratory birds
use an (C)approach called “half-brain sleep.”
This is how it works. Only the left half of the
brain sleeps for a couple of seconds, then only
the right half for the next couple of seconds,
and then this process repeats over and over
again. Isn’t it amazing? Actually, some sea
(D)mammals like dolphins can do that, too,
because they have to keep ⓕto breathe
(E)consciously.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E)의 영영풀이로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: (A): having no interesting parts to notice
(B): to become aware of something even thoughyou cannot see it, hear it, etc.
(C): a road, path, etc. that leads to a place, and isthe main way of reaching it
(D): any animal that gives birth to live young, noteggs, and feeds its young on milk
(E): in a way that shows that you are aware ofor noticing something
solution: (C) approach는 ‘접근법, 방법’이라는 뜻으로 쓰였으나, ‘a road, path, etc. that leads to a place, and is the main way of reaching it(어떤 장소에 이르는, 그리고 그곳에 도달하는 주된 길인 도로, 길 등)’은 approach의 다른 뜻인 ‘진입로, 접근로’에 대한 설명이므로, ‘a method of doing something or dealing with a problem(어떤 것을 하거나 어떤 문제를 다루는 방법)’ 과 같은 설명으로 고쳐야 한다.

Perfectly ⓐshaped tomatoes grow under purple
lighting. Here in the facility, the intensity and timing
of light and the nutrients in the water supply are
all controlled. This indoor vertical farming facility is
able to produce fresh fruit and vegetables all year
round.
Vertical farming refers to ⓑproduce foods in
vertically
stacked
layers
integrated
into
other
structures, usually without the need of soil or
natural light. Since the plants are stacked above
each other, it reduces the amount of space needed
to grow crops.
ⓒOther advantage of indoor vertical farming is
that maintaining the ideal conditions can reduce the
time to harvest. “For traditional farming, if the
climate is good, you have five to six harvests a
year,” says the manager of the facility. “In indoor
farming, we’re now getting roughly 17 harvests out
of that same period.”
There is also the benefit of a reduced need for
water. Any excess water that a plant cannot absorb
will drop down to the plants below. The manager
says the farm uses 95% less water than farming in
a field. “ⓓEvery time water moves through the
system, it’s captured and reused.”
However, indoor vertical farming has an Achilles’
heel: energy consumption. It ⓔhas criticized for the
high energy input it requires. “Solar power could
help bring down energy costs,” the manager says.
“Large scale farms will have solar panels on each
roof. It might support 10 to 15% of our needs.”
This farm wants to fill supply chain gaps rather
than replace outside fields. “Much of our fruit and
vegetables will still be grown under the sun and in
soil, ⓕthat is why it is super important that we also
invest in sustainable field farming,” the manager
says.

water-saving faster harvests through indoorfarming systems

Lab-grown meat is animal flesh grown inside a
laboratory. It is an alternative to red meat obtained
by increasingly unsustainable farming practices. Studies
show that producing lab-grown meat by using
renewable energy would have a significantly lower
carbon footprint than raising farm animals and
making meat products in the most sustainable way.
This is how lab-grown meat is made. To begin
with, lab scientists carefully remove a small number
of cells from an animal. Then, they multiply and
grow the harvested cells, and they produce real
tissue, which is quite similar to conventional meat
in terms of texture and smell. In this way, they can
transform lab-grown cells into steak, chicken breasts,
or hamburger meat. The final product itself is a real
cut of meat, ready to be cooked.

How long does it take for the cells to be growninto a ready-to-cook cut of meat?

solution: Rick Riordan의 모험 소설 「The Lightning Thief」를 바탕으로 영화가 만들어졌다는 소년의 말에 소녀가 속편도 제작되었다 고 답하자 소년이 속편(sequel)의 뜻을 이해하지 못해 ‘What do you mean by a sequel?’(속편이 무슨 뜻이야?)이라고 물었 으며, 이에 소녀가 그것이 이전 영화의 이야기를 이어가는 또 다른 영화를 뜻한다고 설명하는 흐름이므로, 상대방의 의견을 묻는 표현인 ❷ ‘What’s your opinion on a sequel?‘(속편에 대 한 너의 생각은 무엇이니?)과는 바꿔 쓸 수 없다. 참고로, ‘What do you mean by ~?’는 ‘~가 무슨 뜻이야?’라는 뜻으로, 상대방이 한 말 중 이해하지 못한 단어나 표현의 의미를 묻거 나 더 명확한 설명을 요청할 때 쓴다.

(B) 양보 부사절 접속사 though(비록 ~하지만)가 쓰인 부사절 에서 be동사인 is의 보어 역할을 하는 형용사가 though 앞으 로 도치되어 ‘형용사+though+주어+be동사’ 어순을 이루는 구 조가 되어야 하므로, 형용사 humble이 적절하다. (C) 주어 Neither this place nor we에 대한 동사 자리이며, ‘neither A nor B’(A도 B도 아닌) 형태가 주어일 때 nor 뒤의 명 사(구)나 대명사에 동사의 수를 일치시키므로, 대명사 we에 수일 치한 복수동사 deserve가 적절하다.

The second course had to be fruit, and there were
nuts, dried dates, grapes, and apples, for it was
their best season of the year. Baucis even had it in
mind to kill their only goose for dinner, and there
was a great squawking that went on for a long
time. Poor old Baucis wore herself out trying to
catch that goose, but somehow the animal always
got away from her, until the guests made her let it
be, for they had been well served so far. It was a
good meal, and the old couple continued to
encourage their visitors to eat and drink, not caring
that they were now consuming in one day what
would ordinarily have lasted a week.
At last, the wine sank low in the mixing bowl, and
Philemon rose to get some more. (A)그는 그릇이 마
치 이전에 전혀 손대어지지 않았었던 것처럼 다시 가
득 찬 것을 보고 깜짝 놀랐다. Then he whispered to
Baucis that the two strangers must be gods, and
Baucis also was awed and afraid.

Baucis was even planning to serve their onlygoose as dinner for the guests.
The goose escaped from Baucis, and the guests,having already been well treated, told her to letit go.
The elderly couple offered food to the guests butworried that a week’s supply would be gone ina single day.
Philemon whispered to Baucis that there was nodoubt these two strangers were gods.

Ancient cultures recognized the sun’s power to
sustain life, so it was held in a place of honor in
most mythologies.
The Incas who lived in modern day Peru from the
12th to 16th centuries ⓐincorporating the sun in
many aspects of their culture, from holidays to
agriculture. Their sun god, Inti, was one of their
most powerful gods. The Incan royal family was
said to be directly descended from Inti, so his
temples were considered ⓑimportantly. The Temple
of the Sun, in the capital city Cuzco, was made of
carved stone and filled with luxurious gold objects.
In Baltic mythology, the sun was represented by
Saule, the mother and ruler of the world, ⓒwhat
determined the well-being of all life on the earth.
ⓓDepicting as a blonde woman wearing a golden
scarf and a golden crown, Saule lived in a palace at
the end of the sea, where she tended a garden of
golden apples. Saule would ride across the sky in a
chariot pulled by two tireless white horses. Saule
was not the only solar god to ride a vehicle across
the sky. The Greek gods Helios and Apollo were
both shown riding chariots through the heavens.
The Egyptian sun god Ra was said to ride in a
solar boat during the day. At night, he sailed
underwater until he returned to the sky in the east.
The sun has been a central figure in some of the
world’s most enduring myths. That is because there
ⓔwould have been no life without that immense
force in the sky.

body:
“You have spoken well,” said Hermes, “and you
shall have your wish. Yet is there not anything that
you would desire for yourselves?”
At this, the husband glanced over at old Baucis
with her thin, gray hair and her rough hands.
Baucis said, “We have lived together for many
years, and in all that time never has there been a
word of anger between us. Now, at last, we are
growing old and our long companionship is coming
to an end. Grant us this one request, that when we
come to die, we may ⓐperish in the same hour, so
that neither of us would be left without the other.”
She looked at Philemon, and he nodded in
approval, so the old couple turned their eyes on
the gods. “It shall be as you desire,” said Hermes.
“Few would have made such a good and moderate
request.”
Before long, the house became a temple, and the
neighbors, amazed at the change, often came to
ⓑworship and left offerings for the gods. For many
years, Baucis and Philemon lived in peace, passing
from old to extreme old age. At last, they were so
old and bowed that it seemed they could only walk
if they ⓒclung to each other. One evening, it took
them longer than ever to reach the usual spot they
would visit every day to look at the temple. There
they held each other’s arms, thinking that it was
perhaps the last time their limbs would ⓓsupport
them. As they stood, each one felt the other
change and only had time to turn and say
“Farewell,” before they lost their human shapes
completely. Now there stood two tall trees growing
closely side by side with the branches ⓔseparated.
They swayed in the passing breeze as if they
nodded and whispered to each other.

윗글의 분위기로 알맞은 것은?
choices: indifferent and apathetic
tense and suspenseful
chaotic and confusing
touching and noble
ironic and sarcastic
solution: 소원을 말하라는 Hermes에게 노부부는 그들이 한시에 죽어 둘 중 누구도 홀로 남지 않게 해달라고 소원을 빌었고, 신들은 이토록 선하고 적당한 요구를 하는 자는 드물 것이라고 말했 으며, 오랜 시간이 지난 후 어느 날 두 부부는 그들이 바랐던 대로 서로의 팔을 잡은 채로 두 그루의 나무로 변해 영원히 함께 하게 되었다는 내용의 이야기로서, 선한 두 부부의 숭고 한 사랑을 다루고 있으므로, 글의 분위기로 ❹ ‘감동적이고 숭 고한’이 알맞다.

sustain life, so (A)______________________________________.
The Incas who lived in modern day Peru from the
12th to 16th centuries incorporated the sun in
many aspects of their culture, from holidays to
agriculture. Their sun god, Inti, was one of their
most powerful gods. The Incan royal family was
said to be directly descended from Inti, so his
temples
were
considered
ⓐ[insignificant
/
significant]. The Temple of the Sun, in the capital
city Cuzco, was made of carved stone and filled
with luxurious gold objects.
In Baltic mythology, the sun was represented by
Saule, the mother and ruler of the world, who
ⓑ[determined / overlooked] the well-being of all
life on the earth. Depicted as a blonde woman
wearing a golden scarf and a golden crown, Saule
lived in a palace at the end of the sea, where she
tended a garden of golden apples. Saule would ride
across the sky in a chariot pulled by two tireless
white horses. Saule was not the only solar god to
ride a vehicle across the sky. The Greek gods Helios
and
Apollo
were
both
shown
riding
chariots
through the heavens.
The Egyptian sun god Ra was said to ride in a
solar boat during the day. At night, he sailed
underwater until he returned to the sky in the east.
The sun has been a central figure in some of the
world’s most enduring myths. That is because there
would be no life without that ⓒ[minute / immense]
force in the sky.

solution: ⓐ Inti는 잉카의 가장 강력한 신 중 하나였고, 잉카 왕실이 그 의 직계 후손이라 여겨졌으며, 태양의 신전이 조각된 돌로 만 들어지고 호화로운 금으로 채워졌다는 점에서, Inti의 사원이 매우 중요하게 여겨졌다는 흐름으로 significant(중요한)가 적절 하다. ⓑ Saule는 금빛 스카프와 왕관을 착용한 채 바다 끝의 궁전에 살면서 황금 사과 정원을 가꾸고, 두 마리의 지칠 줄 모르는 흰 말이 끄는 전차를 타고 하늘을 가로질렀다고 묘사되므로, 태양이 지구상의 모든 생명의 안녕과 운명을 좌우하는 Saule로 표현되었다는 흐름이 되는 determined(결정했다)가 적절하다. ⓒ 태양이 세상에서 가장 오래 지속되어 온 신화들 중 일부의 중심 소재라는 내용 뒤에 태양을 가리켜 ‘하늘의 거대한 힘’ 없이는 생명체가 존재하지 않았을 것이라고 이유를 제시하는 흐름이 되어야 하므로 immense(거대한)가 적절하다. 천재(강상구) 5과 정답 본 콘텐츠는 해당 출판사로부터 교과서 라이센스를 획득하여 이그잼포유에서 제작하였습니다. 본 콘텐츠에 대한 저작권은 이그잼포유가 소유하고 있으며, 콘텐츠의 전부 또는 일부를 무단 전재하거나 배포하는 것은 저작권법에 의한 법적 책임 을 물을 수 있습니다. 본 콘텐츠의 레이아웃 및 편집에 대한 저작권 침해 행위 또한 금지하고 있습니다. 영어I 천재(강상구) 5과 예상문제 1회 - 객관식(선다형) 1. ② 2. ⑤ 3. ①, ② 4. ① 5. ④ 6. 주관식 7. 주관식 8. ④ 9. ⑤

but would you eat upcycled food? Here are some
innovative restaurants dedicated to reducing food
waste. It is a gorgeous space calling attention to a

extra produce. Here, the pizza is upcycled. It

and made it special. Sustainability is getting more
trendy, and food upcycling is paving the way for

Algae are the fastest growing plant organisms in
nature and a great alternative source of vitamins,
proteins, and minerals. Not only full of nutrients,
they are also easy to grow and don’t take up
precious land space as they are grown in water.
They can grow in places where normal food crops
wouldn’t survive and yield much higher productivity
than crops grown on land. In addition, they create
very rich habitats for plants and animals. On top of
that, algae are very good at trapping carbon
themselves, which helps slow down global warming.

Perfectly shaped tomatoes grow under purple
lighting. Here in the facility, ⓐthe intensity and
timing of light and the nutrients in the water
supply is all controlled. This indoor vertical farming
facility is able to produce fresh fruit and vegetables
all year round.
Vertical farming refers to producing foods in
vertically
stacked
layers
integrated
into
other
structures, usually without the need of soil or
natural light. Since the plants are stacked above
each other, it reduces the amount of space
(A)[needing / needed] to grow crops.
Another advantage of indoor vertical farming is
that maintaining the ideal conditions can reduce the
time to harvest. “For traditional farming, if the
climate is good, you have five to six harvests a
year,” ⓑsaying the manager of the facility. “In
indoor farming, we’re now getting roughly 17
harvests out of that same period.”
There is also the benefit of a reduced need for
water. Any excess water that a plant cannot absorb
will drop down to the plants below. The manager
says (B)[that / what] the farm uses 95% less water
than farming in a field. “Every time water moves
through the system, it’s captured and reused.”
However, indoor vertical farming has an Achilles’
heel: energy consumption. It has been criticized for
the high energy input it requires. “Solar power
could help (C)[bringing / to bring] down energy
costs,” the manager says. “Large scale farms will
have solar panels on each roof. It might support 10
to 15% of our needs.”
This farm wants to ⓒ_________________________________
________________. “Much of our fruit and vegetables
will still be grown under the sun and in soil, which
is why it is super important that we also invest in
sustainable field farming,” the manager says.

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: needing  that      bringing

needing  what      to bring

solution: (A) 문장의 동사로 reduces가 쓰였으므로 흐름상 앞의 명사 (space)를 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 하 며, space(공간)가 ‘필요하게 되는’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 지닌 과거분사 needed가 알맞다. (B) 완전한 절(the farm ~ field)을 이끌어 동사 says의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로, 명사절 접속사 that이 알맞다. 참고로, what은 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 또는 의문대명사로 쓰이며, 불완전한 절을 이끌어 문장에서 주어, 목적어, 보어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이룬다. (C) ‘~하는 데 도움이 되다, ~하는 것을 돕다’라는 뜻으로 ‘help+동사원형/to부정사’를 쓸 수 있으므로, could help 뒤에 to부정사인 to bring이 알맞다.

body:
Jo: Hello, listeners. ⓐ여러분은 밤에 여러분 머리 바
로 위로 대규모 이동이 일어날 때가 있다는 것을
아셨나요? The scale of migration involving
billions of birds traveling up to thousands of
kilometers leaves you in (A)[awe / boredom]. On
today’s Jo’s Tea Time, we invite naturalist and
author Scott Weidensaul to share his knowledge.
He’s spent decades studying migratory birds,
writing
about
them,
and
engaging
in
conservation efforts. Welcome to the show, Mr.
Weidensaul.
Weidensaul: Thanks for having me, Jo.
Jo: Your new book says every spring and fall,
hundreds of millions to billions of migratory
birds pass over our roofs, but we seem to
have no idea that it’s happening. Why is that?
Weidensaul: Well, most birds migrate after dark,
including almost all of the birds that are
normally active during the day. That’s why it’s
(B)[easy / hard] for us to realize the migration is
happening. They migrate at night because the
night sky is cooler, and the air calmer. Besides,
there are (C)[fewer / more] predators at night. If
you could strip away the night sky and make
everything visible, this migration would probably
be the largest, greatest natural spectacle on the
planet.
Jo: Among those global travelers in your book, I
found the bar-tailed godwits to be particularly
impressive.
Weidensaul: Sure. Some of them can even make a
10,000 km non-stop journey across the Pacific
Ocean, from western Alaska to New Zealand in
11 days.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: awehardmore
boredomeasymore
awehardfewer
aweeasyfewer
boredomhardfewer
solution: (A) 수십억 마리의 새들이 수천 킬로미터까지 여행하는 철새 이동의 규모에 대한 감상이므로, 그것이 경외감을 자아낸다는 흐름이 되는 awe(경외감)가 알맞다. (B) 보통 낮에 활동하는 거의 모든 새를 포함하여 대부분의 새 들이 어두워진 후에 이동한다고 했으므로, 이것의 결과로서 우 리가 이런 이동이 일어난다는 걸 알아차리기 어렵다는 흐름이 되는 hard(어려운)가 알맞다. (C) 새들이 밤에 이동하는 것은 밤하늘이 더 시원하고 공기가 더 잔잔하기 때문이라는 내용 다음에 접속부사 Besides(게다 가)에 연결된 추가적인 이유가 이어져야 하므로, 밤에는 포식 자도 더 적다는 흐름이 되는 fewer(더 적은)가 알맞다. 천재(강상구) 4과

body:
Weidensaul: Birds in migratory condition can do
things that they can’t do at other times of the
year. (A)[Other / Another] neat trick you might
envy is that they can gain a tremendous amount
of muscle tissue without exercise. For example,
before some bar-tailed godwits leave Alaska in
September and make a 10,000 km flight across
the Pacific, they undergo a process of binge
feeding. They just eat and eat until they double
their weight. By the time they take off, their
heart and flight muscles may have increased by
50%. After they (B)[had / have] eaten as much as
they possibly can and can’t put any more weight
on, their digestive organs shrink dramatically
because these won’t (C)[put / be put] to use
during the non-stop flight to New Zealand.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)           (B)          (C)
choices: Otherhavebe put
Anotherhadput
Otherhadbe put
Anotherhaveput
Anotherhavebe put
solution: (A) 뒤에 단수가산명사구 neat trick이 이어지므로, ‘또 하나의 ~’라는 뜻으로 단수가산명사(구)를 수식하는 Another가 알맞 다. 참고로, other는 ‘다른 ~(들)’의 뜻으로 뒤에 복수가산명사 (구)나 불가산명사(구)가 이어진다. (B) and로 이어진 절에서 더 이상 몸무게가 늘지 않는다는 내용이 현재시제(can’t)로 진술되어 있으며 그 이전의 과거 시점부터 기준이 되는 현재 시점까지 먹을 수 있는 한 많이 먹은 상태라는 의미가 되어야 하므로, 현재완료(have[has]+p.p.)를 이루는 have가 알맞다. (C) because가 이끄는 절의 주어 these가 ‘their digestive organs(그들의 소화 기관들)’를 가리키며, ’활용되는‘ 대상이고 뒤에 목적어 없이 전치사 to와 명사 use가 이어지므로, ‘put ~ to use(~을 활용하다)’의 수동태인 ‘be put to use(~가 활용되 다)’를 이루는 be put이 알맞다.

in one of Europe’s most beautiful capital cities,
Vienna. Now it’s home to nearly 2 million people,
but 50% of the city is green space. ⓐWhat I’m
looking for is probably one of Europe’s most
critically endangered mammals.
Now, I’ve come really early to a graveyard to try
to see some hamsters because this is one of the
best ⓑtimes of day to see them. At this time of
the day, there’s nobody around so they don’t have
to avoid people while looking for food. These little
ones have been in the area for decades, but now
ⓒlive among the dead because development has
robbed them of the green fields they used to
inhabit.
Look! I just found ⓓones over there. See how it
is trying to stuff its cheeks full? Hamsters can pack
a quarter of their body weight inside their cheeks,
which
helps
them
get
through
the
winter.
Surprisingly, they not only feed on nuts and
flowers, but have also adapted to eating candle
wax, which is a good source of fat and is easy to
find in graveyards.
Even though the hamsters here have adapted to
the noises of the city, they still (A)___________________
______________, as predators are never too far away.
They may need to quickly escape back down into
their holes, which are complex structures stretching
under the ground. Despite urban areas generally
ⓔhaving a negative effect on wildlife, cities can
actually provide islands of protection for it.

choices: keep a watchful eye
store food for winter
rely on humans for their food supply
suppress their natural instinct to hide
prefer living in an urban environment
solution: 정답은 ① 이다. (해설 없음)

How do we open ourselves up to new possibilities?
One of the ways to do this is to connect things
that look ⓐseparately. This can be incredibly
pleasing as it helps us to see the world in a
different light and gain a greater appreciation for
the interrelation of all things. Here are three artists
who are willing to experiment with this approach.
Beyond the Scene
Meet Robin Yayla, a visual storyteller ⓑlives in
Milan, Italy, who has been delighting his viewers
with his unique artworks on social media. He draws
illustrations on top of photos of landmarks or
buildings and offers whole new ways to see them.
To breathe life into well-known structures around the
world, he often uses iconic pop culture characters.
His unique twists sometimes turn ⓒthat we
consider dull and boring into something delightful.
To him, a bridge is a net, and a road is a bowling
lane. After finding ⓓwhatever is common in two
unrelated things, he connects them smoothly in his
digital drawing.
His work combines his passion for traveling and
drawing. Exploring new places and learning about
new cultures inspire his artistic mind to come up
with new ideas for his art. Many of his digital
illustrations transform the most historic buildings of
the world into new objects that you would like to
see again. For example, he added images of ice
cream cones onto the scenic photo of St. Basil’s
Cathedral in Moscow, the capital of Russia. The
Leaning Tower of Pisa, one of the most remarkable
architectural ⓔstructures in Italy, appeared to be a
camera lens to him.

Robin Yayla looks for shared features betweentwo different things before connecting them inhis artwork.

body:
Fun Shadows
When we look at shadows of objects in real life,
most of us think nothing of them. Belgian artist
and film-maker Vincent Bal, however, turns them
into art forms. He lets his creativity flow to make
beautiful and meaningful scenes with shadows.
His playful shadow art illustrations are made by
ⓐadding his own doodles to shadows cast from
everyday objects, like a flower or a glass. In one
image, the shadow from a key is reinterpreted as a
DJ wearing headphones. In another, a potato peeler
creates the perfectly shaped frame for a piano. In
his art, the shadow from a glass becomes a pool.
He uses a very simple process to draw his
pictures. ㉠그 과정을 시작하기 위해, 그가 할 필요가
있는 일은 평범한 물건, 종이 한 장, 그리고 조명을 준
비하는 것뿐이다. Then he puts the object on the
paper and turns on the light. He just starts moving
the light around and places the object in different
positions. He keeps a very (A)[open / closed] mind
and tries not to have an idea in advance about
what the result should be.
“If I try to shape a shadow into a certain form, it
always feels a bit forced. If nothing comes, I take
another object, and then I just start playing around
with it until suddenly I see something. In this way, I
can create ⓑwhatever I want,” he says. His free
artistic interpretation of shadows means that the
possibilities for creating new doodles are (B)[endless
/ restricted].
In fact, it was by accident ⓒwhich he started
making his art pieces. While he was working on a
new script, he suddenly noticed how the shadow of
a cup on his desk looked like a little elephant. He
completed the image with a few lines, took a
picture and shared it on the Internet. The reactions
were so positive that he challenged ⓓhim to make
one shadow image every day.
Art can inspire you to see the world from a(n)
(C)[new / existing] angle. Connecting ideas that at
first glance appear ⓔunrelated is a powerful tool
for exploring the beauty of the world around us. To
make such connections, all you need is your
imaginative power.

I became a book artist almost ⓐby accident. After
graduating in 2003, I traveled to Thailand. At that
time, I didn’t think about working with books.
Shopping in Bangkok, I came across a used book
with beautiful notes written in it. That got me
interested in the way ⓑpaper was used in art. Soon
after I returned to the UK, my father passed away.
Feeling ⓒsorrowful, I found myself picking up the
Graham Greene classic I had brought back from my
trip and cutting paper moths out of the pages. I
then hung them over the open book. Since then, I
have created sculptures out of books.
I always read the story first to get ⓓillusion, and
everything for the sculpture is made from the
pages
within
that
book;
some
don’t
have
illustrations, so I take inspiration from the title and
the text. I am also drawn toward fairy tales,
especially Hans Christian Andersen’s; his tales are
quite magical, but there’s also a sadness as they
don’t always have a happy ending.
For me, books are not only sources of ideas and
associations, but also objects of great beauty to be
cut up and rearranged. I use very simple tools: a
sharp knife, a bit of glue, and some wire. ⓔUtilizing
the open book as my base, I cut its pages, glue
them, gently pull them up, and support them with
wire. Through these processes, I construct physical
representations of the narratives and the characters.

M: Daedalus and his son Icarus were kept in a tall
tower by King Minos. To escape from the tower,
Daedalus made two pairs of giant wings out of
wax and feathers. As he attached the wings to
his son, he gave a warning. Flying too near the
ocean would make the wings wet and make
them too heavy to use. Flying too close to the
sun, the heat would melt the wax, and the wings
would fall apart. In either case, they surely would
die. Therefore, the key to their escape would be
in keeping to the middle. With the instructions
clear, both men left from the tower. They were
the first men ever to fly. While Daedalus flew
safely between the sun and the ocean, Icarus
was so excited that he forgot his father’s warning.
Daedalus could only watch in horror as Icarus flew
up higher and higher, powerless to change his
son’s fate. When the heat from the sun melted
the wax on his wings, Icarus fell from the sky.

다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

Ancient cultures recognized the sun’s power to
sustain life, so it was held in a place of honor in
most mythologies.
The Incas who lived in modern day Peru from the
12th to 16th centuries incorporated the sun in
many aspects of their culture, from holidays to
agriculture. Their sun god, Inti, was one of their
most powerful gods. The Incan royal family was
said to be directly descended from Inti, so his
temples were considered important. The Temple of
the Sun, in the capital city Cuzco, was made of
carved stone and filled with luxurious gold objects.
In Baltic mythology, the sun was represented by
Saule, the mother and ruler of the world, who
determined the well-being of all life on the earth.
Depicted as a blonde woman wearing a golden
scarf and a golden crown, Saule lived in a palace at
the end of the sea, where she tended a garden of
golden apples. Saule would ride across the sky in a
chariot pulled by two tireless white horses. Saule
was not the only solar god to ride a vehicle across
the sky. The Greek gods Helios and Apollo were
both shown riding chariots through the heavens.
The Egyptian sun god Ra was said to ride in a
solar boat during the day. At night, he sailed
underwater until he returned to the sky in the east.
The sun has been a central figure in some of the
world’s most enduring myths. That is because there
would be no life without that immense force in the
sky.
choices: In many myths, the sun, which holds the powerto sustain life, appeared as a revered presence.
Since the Inca royal family was considered thedirect descendants of Inti, his temples were heldin great importance.
In Baltic mythology, the sun was seen as Saule, amotherandsovereignwhooversawthewell-being of all life on Earth.
Saule, Helios, and Apollo are all sun gods depictedas riding a chariot across the sky.
Despite its importance, the sun has long beenregarded as a negative presence in many ancientmyths.

B: I need something sweet. I think I’ll have some
chocolate.
G: You’re a huge chocolate lover, aren’t you?
B: You can say that again. I can’t imagine my life
without chocolate.
G: I see, but did you know that you might not be
able to have it in the future?
B: What are you talking about?
G: Because of global warming, some foods are
endangered, and believe it or not, chocolate is
one of them.
B: What? No way! I had no idea that global warming
would affect my life so much.
G: (A)I think we really should pay attention to
environmental issues in everyday life.
B: You said it.

I think we really are willing to pay attention
solution: 밑줄 친 ‘I think we really should pay attention’은 ‘나는 우리가 정말 주의를 기울여야 한다고 생각해’라는 뜻으로, 지구 온난화 가 자신의 삶에 이렇게 큰 영향을 줄 것이라는 생각을 하지 못 했다는 상대방의 말에 환경 문제에 대해 좀 더 주의를 기울이자 고 제안 또는 권유하는 의미로 쓰였으므로, 의향이나 의지에 대 한 생각을 나타내는 ❺ ‘I think we really are willing to pay attention’(나는 우리가 정말 주의를 기울일 의향이 있다고 생각 해)과는 바꿔 쓸 수 없다.

Industrial food systems generate more than one
third of all greenhouse gas emissions. The processes
we rely on to produce, transport, and store meals and
raw ingredients, not to mention the landfills covered
with food waste, are speeding up climate change.
Animal-based foods, including red meat, milk products,
and farmed shrimp, are generally associated with the
highest greenhouse gas emissions. Especially, our
meat
production
accelerates
global
warming
significantly, uses shrinking supplies of fresh water,
destroys forests and grasslands, and damages soil.

alternatives to our current diets. Let us explore
some ways we could be eating in the near future.

3D food printing has the potential to save the
environment, while revolutionizing food production;
for example, it can convert alternative ingredients
such as proteins from insects into delicious meals.
The underlying concept for food printing is the
same as any other 3D printing. In 3D food printing,
various inks ― liquid forms of food ― are placed
one layer at a time to build complex 3D constructs
with full textures and customized nutrients.
3D food printing can be readily undertaken in
many parts of the globe. Various food inks with
adequate nutrients and favorable flavors can be
sent to areas that are hard to get to, where food
can be printed on site. In this way, 3D printed food
with necessary nutrients can be provided for large
populations in areas affected by a natural disaster
or a crisis developed by humans.

panels on each roof. It might support 10 to 15% of
our needs.”
This farm wants to fill supply chain gaps rather
than replace outside fields. “Much of our fruit and
vegetables will still be grown under the sun and in
soil, which is why it is super important that we also
invest in sustainable field farming,” the manager says.

Perfectly shaped tomatoes grow under purple
lighting. Here in the facility, the intensity and timing
of light and the nutrients in the water supply are all
controlled. This indoor vertical farming facility is able
to produce fresh fruit and vegetables all year round.
Vertical farming refers to producing foods in
vertically
stacked
layers
integrated
into
other

natural light. Since the plants are stacked above
each other, it (A)[cuts / increases] the amount of

Another (B)[advantage / disadvantage] of indoor
vertical
farming
is
that
maintaining
the
ideal
conditions can reduce the time to harvest. “For
traditional farming, if the climate is good, you have
five to six harvests a year,” says the manager of the
facility. “In indoor farming, we’re now getting
roughly 17 harvests out of that same period.”
There is also the benefit of a reduced need for
water. Any excess water that a plant cannot absorb
will drop down to the plants below. The manager
says the farm uses 95% less water than farming in
a field. “Every time water moves through the
system, it’s captured and reused.”
However, indoor vertical farming has an Achilles’
heel: energy consumption. It has been (C)[praised /
criticized] for the high energy input it requires.
“Solar power could help bring down energy costs,”
the manager says. “Large scale farms will have solar
panels on each roof. It might support 10 to 15% of
our needs.”
This farm wants to fill supply chain gaps rather
than replace outside fields. “Much of our fruit and
vegetables will still be grown under the sun and in
soil, which is why it is super important that we also
invest in sustainable field farming,” the manager says.

대한 생각을 나타 내는 ⑤ ‘I think we really are willing to pay attention’ (나는 우리가 정말 주의를 기울일 의향이 있다고 생각해) 과는 바꿔 쓸 수 없다. 참고로, ‘I think we should ~’(나 는 우리가 ~해야 한다고 생각해)는 ‘I believe we should ~’(나는 우리가 ~해야 한다고 믿어 ② 나는 우리가 정말 주의를 기울여야 한다고 생각해 ③ 내 생각으로는, 우리는 주의를 기울여야 해 ④ 나는 우리가 정말 주의를 기울여야 한다고 생각해 2) ⑤: 우리가 일상생활에서 환경 문제에 정말 주의를 기울여야 한다고 생각한다는 소녀의 말에 소년이 ‘You said it.’(맞 는 말이야.)이라고 답하며 동조하고 있으므로, ⑤ ‘소년은 우리가 매일 (→밀가루) 9) ②, ③ : ⓑ what → which (앞의 주절(algae are ~ themselves)에 접속사 없이 쉼표(,)로만 이어져 있으며, 동사 helps의 의미 상 주어가 주절이 나타내는 내용에 해당하므로, 주절을 부 연 설명하는 관계사절을 이끄는 주격 관계대명사를 써야 한다. 따라서 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 what을 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which로 고친다. 그 외, 앞 절 전 체가 선행사인 경우 단수 취급하므로 단수동사인 helps로 수일치 시킨 것과, ‘~하는 데 도움이 되다’라는 뜻으로 ‘help+동사원형/to부정사’를 사용하므로 helps 뒤에 ‘~의 속도를 늦추다’라는 뜻의 구동사 ‘slow ~ down’이 동사원 형 slow로 시작해 쓰이고, 부사 뒤에 목적어인 명사구 global warming이 이어진 것은 모두 적절하다.) ⓒ This → It (지시대명사 This가 가리키는 지시 대상이 앞에 없으며, 흐름상 to부정사구인 ‘to change ~ climate’ 가 문장의 주어이므로 ‘가주어(It)-진주어(to부정사구)’ 구문 을 이루도록 대명사 This를 가주어 It으로 고친다.) 오답 ⓓ 주어 we를 강조하기 위해 쓰인 강조 용법의 재귀대명 사 ourselves와, 주어에 수일치 시킨 복수동사 need에 ‘~ 할 필요가 있다’라는 뜻의 ‘need+to부정사(구)’를 이루는 to부정사 to start는 모두 적절하다. 10) ②: (A) 조류는 영양이 풍부할 뿐 아니라 재배하기도 쉽고, 소중한 육지의 공간을 차지하지도 않으며, 일반 작물이 생존할 수 없는 곳에서 자랄 수 있고 높은 생산성을 낸다는 내용 뒤에, 동식물에게 매우 영양이 풍부한 서 식지를 만들어 준다는 추가적인 장점이 이어지므로, 빈 칸에는 ‘게다가’라는 뜻의 In addition, 또는 ‘또한’이라 는 뜻의 Also가 알맞다. (B) 식단을 바꾸는 것은 큰 과제이고, 모든 사람이 한 걸음 앞으로 나아가지는 않을 것이라는 내용 뒤에, 식 량 수요의 증가와 지구 온난화에 미치는 영향을 볼 때, 우리 자신이 식단 변화를 고려해야 한다는 대조적인 내용이 이어지므로, 빈칸에는 ‘그러나’라는 뜻의 However 가 알맞다. 오답 ① 결과적으로 그러나 ③ 따라서 대조적으로 ④ 또한 예를 들어 ⑤ 결론적으로 예를 들어 11) ②: 음식 인쇄의 근본적인 개념은 다른 3차원 인쇄와 동일 하다고 했으므로, ② ‘음식 인쇄는 다른 3차원 인쇄와 는 완전히 다른 개념을 사용한다.’는 일치하지 않는 내 용이다. 오답 ① 3차원 음식 인쇄는 곤충 단백질을 맛있는 식사로 바꿀 수 있다. ③ 액체 형태의 음식 잉크는 질감과 맞춤형 영양소를 지닌 복잡한 음식을 만든다. ④ 음식 잉크는 외진 지역에 보내져 현장에서 인쇄될 수 있다. ⑤ 3차원 인쇄 음식은 재해나 인간에 의해 만들어진 위기 후에 사람들을 먹여 살릴 수 있다. 12) This means that, to feed everyone, it will take, more food than is produced in the world : • 주어로 대명사 This, 동사로 주어에 수일치한 단수동사 means를 쓴다. • 제시된 that을 명사절 접속사로 활용해 뒤에 완전한 절 을 연결하여 means의 목적어절을 쓴다. • ‘~을 먹여 살리기 위해’를 나타내기 위해 ‘목적’을 나타 내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to feed를 쓴다. • ‘~하는 데 …가 든다[필요하다]’라는 뜻의 ‘it takes … to 부정사’ 구조를 사용하되, 제시된 조동사 will과 동사원형 take를 사용해 미래시제로 쓴다. • ‘더 많은 식량’을 나타내기 위해 형용사 much를 비교급 인 more로 변형하여 수식 대상인 명사 food 앞에 쓴다. • than이 제시되어 있으므로, 주어가 없는 불완전한 절을 이끌어 선행사 more food(더 많은 식량)를 수식하는 관계 사절을 이루는 유사관계대명사로 활용하되, 선행사의 핵심 단어인 단수명사 food가 ‘생산되는’ 대상이므로, produce 를 단수형 수동태인 is produced로 변형하여 쓴다. 13) we rely on to produce, transport, and store, not to mention, covered with food waste, are speeding up : • 목적격 관계대명사를 생략하라는 <조건>에 따라, ‘자동 사+전치사’ 구조의 구동사 ‘rely on ~’(~에 의존하다)에서 전치사 on의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절이 명사구 The processes(공정들)를 꾸미도록 영작한다. • ‘~을 생산, 운송, 보관하기 위해’를 나타내기 위해 <조 건>에 따라 ‘목적’을 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사를 활용하고, 빈칸 수에 맞춰 to부정사의 to에 이어 동사원형 produce, transport, store가 ‘A, B, and C’의 구조로 병렬 연결을 이루도록 to produce, transport, and store로 쓴다. • mention이 제시되어 있으므로, ‘~은 말할 것도 없고’를 뜻하는 독립부정사 ‘not to mention ~’을 활용한다. • 명사구 the landfills(매립지들)를 수식하는 분사구를 활 용하되, 수식 대상인 명사구가 ‘(~로) 뒤덮인’ 대상이므로, ‘cover ~ with …’(~을 …로 뒤덮다)의 수동 표현인 ‘~ be covered with …’(~가 …로 뒤덮이다)에서 과거분사 covered와 전치사 with를 사용한다. • <보기>에 be가 제시되어 있으므로 ‘더 빠르게 하고 있 다’라는 의미로 ‘am/are/is+현재분사’ 형태의 현재진행형 을 사용하되, 주어부의 핵심 단어인 processes가 복수명 사이므로 이에 수일치된 복수동사 are를 쓰고, ‘~을 빨라 지게 하다’를 뜻하는 구동사 ‘speed ~ up’에서 동사 speed를 현재분사 speeding으로 변형한 뒤 up을 이어서 쓴다. 14) ②: ⓑ higher(더 높은) → lower(더 적은) 15) ⑤: 앞에서 곤충들은 단백질의 생산에 가축보다 훨씬 더 적 은 자원을 사용하고 음식물 쓰레기에서도 길러질 수 있 다고 했으므로, 결과적으로 곤충들의 사육을 비용 효과 가 높게 만든다는 흐름이 되는 ⑤ ‘그것들을 기르는 것 을 매우 비용 효율이 높게 만든다’가 빈칸에 알맞다. 본문변형 makes raising them very cost-effective → makes it very cost-effective to raise them 오답 ① 그 단백질을 먹기에 안전하지 않게 만든다 ② 생산 비용을 급격히 증가시킨다 ③ 사육을 소수의 부유한 나라들로 제한한다 ④ 많은 양의 깨끗한 물을 필요로 한다 16) ④: 기아와 기후 변화에 맞서 싸우는 데 있어 곤충을 단백 질원으로 활용하는 것의 중요성과 장점으로, 가축보다 훨씬 더 적은 자원으로 단백질을 생산해 비용 효율이 높다는 점과, 곤충이 가지는 부정적인 인상이라는 주요 장벽이 있으나 그것의 외양을 바꿈으로써 극복할 수 있다는 점을 다루고 있으므로, 글의 주제로 ④ ‘지속 가 능한 곤충 단백질과 부정적인 인상 극복하기’가 알맞다. 오답 ① 일상 식품 속 곤충 가루, 밀가루, 그리고 기름 ② 음식물 쓰레기를 사용하는 저자원 곤충 사육 ③ 곤충 섭취의 오랜 역사와 전 세계적 확산 ⑤ 곤충 제품을 저지하는 대중의 혐오감과 질병 공포 17) ⑤: 2050년까지 세계 인구가 100억 명 정도로 늘어날 것으 로 예상된다는 주어진 글에 이어, 이를 This로 받아 이 것은 56% 더 많은 식량이 필요하다는 것을 의미하지만 안타깝게도 대부분의 나라에서 섭취하는 종류의 식단을 뒷받침할 가용 농지가 충분하지 않다는 문제점을 제기 하는 (C), 제한된 농지 문제를 this로 받아 이것뿐 아니 라 산업화된 식품 체계가 전체 온실가스 배출량의 3분 의 1 이상을 발생시키고 음식과 원재료의 생산, 운송, 보관을 위해 의존하는 공정들이 기후 변화를 더 빠르게 하고 있다는 추가적인 문제점을 제시하는 (B), 동물성 식품이 대체로 가장 많은 온실가스 배출과 관련이 있으 며 육류 생산이 지구 온난화의 가속화, 담수 공급원의 소모, 삼림과 목초지의 파괴, 토양 훼손의 문제를 발생 시킨다고 부연 설명하는 (A)의 흐름이 자연스럽다. 18) ④: (A) 앞에서 식물들이 서로의 위에 쌓여 있다고 했으므 로, 결과적으로 수직 농업은 농작물을 기르는 데 필요 한 공간의 양을 줄인다는 흐름이 되는 cuts(~을 줄인 다)가 알맞다. increase ~을 늘리다 본문변형 reduces → cuts (B) 앞에서 (실내) 수직 농업의 이점으로 공간의 양을 줄인다고 했으며, 이상적인 조건을 유지하는 것이 수확 까지 걸리는 시간을 줄일 수 있다는 내용이 이어지므 로, 실내 수직 농업의 또 다른 이점이라는 흐름이 되는 advantage(장점)가 알맞다. disadvantage 단점 (C) 앞에서 실내 수직 농업에는 에너지 소비라는 약점 이 있다고 했으므로, 그것이 요구하는 높은 에너지 투 입에 대해 비난받아 왔다는 흐름이 되는 criticized(비난 받는)가 알맞다. praise ~을 칭찬하다 19) (1) the intensity and timing of light and the nutrients in the water supply (2) uses 95% less water (than farming in a field) 질문 (1) 수직 농업 시설은 농작물을 일 년 내내 기르기 위해 무 엇을 통제하는가? → 그것은 조명의 강도와 시기, 그리고 공급되는 물의 영양 분을 통제한다. (2) 실내 수직 농장은 들판에서의 농업보다 물을 얼마나 더 적게 사용하는가? → 그것은 (들판에서의 농업보다) 물을 95% 더 적게 사용 한다. 20) ④: 식단은 복잡하고 문화적 영향을 받으며, 기후에 끼치는 영향을 줄이기 위해 식단을 바꾸는 것은 큰 과제이기에 한 걸음 나아가기가 쉽지는 않지만, 식량 수요의 증가 와 지구 온난화에 미치는 영향을 볼 때 우리의 식단에 변화를 줄 것을 고려해야 하며, 이제는 낯선 것에 익숙 해질 때라는 내용이므로, 글의 제목으로 ④ ‘식습관을 바꾸기는 어렵지만, 기후가 그것을 요구한다’가 알맞다. 오답 ① 일상 식단에서 증가하고 있는 낯선 음식들 ② 문화는 식단을 결정지으며, 우리에게 더 나은 선택 지를 준다 ③ 식단 변화는 모두에게 아주 쉽다 as easy as falling off a log 아주 쉬운 ⑤ 지구 온난화의 속도를 늦추기 위해 문화적으로 형성 된 식단으로 바꾸기

body:
다음 주어진 대화에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?

G: Hey, what are you up to?
B: I have to write an essay about my weakest point
and how to overcome it.
G: Oh, yeah? Then, what’s your “Achilles’ heel”?
(A) What did you do to overcome it?
(B) An “Achilles’ heel” is an area of weakness. It
comes from the Greek myth of Achilles.
(C) For me, breaking down a large task into smaller
ones and setting deadlines for each one really
helped.
(D) You know what? That’s a pretty common problem.
I used to have that problem, too.
(E) What do you mean by “Achilles’ heel”?
(F) Oh, I see. Then I’d say my Achilles’ heel is that I
always put things off until the last minute.
B: That’s a good idea. I’ll definitely give it a try.
solution: 소녀가 소년에게 안부를 묻자, 소년은 자신의 약점과 그것을 극복하는 방법에 대한 에세이를 써야 한다고 말하고, 소녀가 소년의 “Achilles’ heel”이 무엇인지 물어보는 주어진 대화에 이 어, “Achilles’ heel”이라는 표현이 무엇을 의미하는지 묻는 (E), 질문에 대한 답으로 “Achilles’ heel”의 정의와 배경 설명을 한 (B), 의미를 이해한 후 자신의 “Achilles’ heel”은 항상 마지막 순간까지 일을 미루는 것이라고 말한 (F), 상대방의 “Achilles’ heel”을 that problem(그 문제)으로 가리켜 자신도 그 문제를 가지고 있었다고 말한 (D), that problem(그 문제)을 it(그것)으 로 가리켜 그것을 극복하기 위해 무엇을 했는지 묻는 (A), 문 제 해결에 도움이 되었던 자신의 방법을 말한 (C)로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다.

body:
다음 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

B: We’re going bowling next Tuesday, right?
G: Actually, it’s Thursday. By the way, did you know
that Thursday originated from “Thor’s day”?
B: Thor? You mean the main character of the movie
series?
G: Yeah. You know, he’s a figure from a myth.
B: Really? I thought he was just a movie character.
G: Actually, there are some differences between the
Thor in the movie and the Thor in the myth.
B: Like what?
G: Take Thor’s hammer for example. In the myth, the
hammer is a powerful weapon that can control
the weather, but in the movie, it also lets him
fly.
B: Wow, you must be a big Thor fan. You seem to
know a lot about him.
G: Yes, he is my favorite character in that movie.
Who’s your favorite character in the series?
B: Let me see. I would have to say that Loki’s my
favorite. I love his clever little tricks.
G: Yeah, he’s charming.
choices: The girl is planning to go bowling nextThursday.
The boy knew Thor only as a character fromthe movie.
The girl clearly understands the differences inThor’s hammer between the movie and themyth.
The girl prefers the Thor from the movie overthe Thor from the myth.
The boy’s favorite character in the movie seriesis Loki, who plays clever tricks.
solution: 소녀는 영화 속에서 Thor의 열렬한 팬으로 Thor가 가장 좋아 하는 캐릭터라고 말하고 있지만 신화 속 Thor와 비교해서 말 하고 있지 않으므로, ❹ ‘소녀는 신화 속 Thor보다 영화 속 Thor를 더 선호한다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다. 천재(강상구) 5과

body:
However, the gods smiled kindly at them and
identified themselves as Zeus and Hermes. Hermes
said, “Both of you welcomed us beneath your roof
this day when others refused us shelter. ⓐBe sure
those shall be punished who would not help the
wandering strangers, but you shall have whatever
reward you ㉠[choose / are chosen]. Tell us what
you will have.”
(A) She looked at Philemon, and he nodded in
approval, so the old couple turned their eyes
on the gods. “It shall be as you desire,” said
Hermes. “Few would have made such a good
and moderate request.” Before long, the house
became a temple, and the neighbors, ⓑamazed
at the change, often came to worship and left
offerings for the gods. For many years, Baucis
and Philemon lived in peace, ㉡[passed /
passing] from old to extreme old age.
(B) “You have spoken well,” said Hermes, “and you
shall have your wish. Yet is there not anything
that you would desire for yourselves?” At this,
the husband glanced over at old Baucis with
her thin, gray hair and her rough hands. Baucis
said, “We have lived together for many years,
and in all that time never has there been a
word of anger between us. Now, at last, we
are growing old and our long companionship
is coming to an end. Grant us this one
request, that when we come to die, we may
perish in the same hour, so that neither of us
would be left without the other.”
(C) The old man thought for a little while ⓒwith
his eyes bent on the ground, and then he
said: “We have lived happily together here for
many years, even though the times have been
hard. But never ㉢[have we turned / we have
turned] strangers away or asked for a reward
for entertaining them. ⓓTo have spoken with
the immortals face to face is a thing few men
can boast of. In this small cottage, ⓔhumble
though it is, the gods have sat at meal.
Neither this place nor we deserve the honor.
If, therefore, you will do something for us, turn
this cottage into a temple where the gods
may always be served and where we may live
out the rest of our days.”

body:
Ancient cultures recognized the sun’s power to
sustain life, so it was held in a place of honor in
most mythologies.
The Incas who lived in modern day Peru from the
12th to 16th centuries incorporated the sun in
many aspects of their culture, from holidays to
agriculture. Their sun god, Inti, was one of their
most powerful gods. (A) The Incan royal family was
said to be directly descended from Inti, so his
temples were considered important. (B) The Temple
of the Sun, in the capital city Cuzco, was made of
carved stone and filled with luxurious gold objects.
(C) In Baltic mythology, the sun was represented
by Saule, the mother and ruler of the world, who
determined the well-being of all life on the earth.
(D) Moreover, Baltic mythology was formed and
developed over generations, being passed down
through folk songs, legends, and oral storytelling
rather than written records. (E) Depicted as a blonde
woman wearing a golden scarf and a golden crown,
Saule lived in a palace at the end of the sea,
where she tended a garden of golden apples. Saule
would ride across the sky in a chariot pulled by
two tireless white horses. Saule was not the only
solar god to ride a vehicle across the sky. The
Greek gods Helios and Apollo were both shown
riding chariots through the heavens.
The Egyptian sun god Ra was said to ride in a
solar boat during the day. At night, he sailed
underwater until he returned to the sky in the east.
The sun has been a central figure in some of the
world’s most enduring myths. That is because
ⓐ_____________________________________________________.

solution: ⓐ 노부부가 좋은 음식과 하나밖에 없는 거위를 대접하려고 했고, 일주일은 갈 음식량을 하루에 소진하는 것도 개의치 않 을 만큼 계속해서 손님들에게 먹고 마시기를 권유하며 극진히 손님들을 대접했다는 흐름이므로, 부정어 not 뒤에 caring(신 경 쓰면서)이 적절하다. ⓑ 포도주가 그릇 바닥까지 줄었다가 애초에 손대지 않았던 것처럼 다시 채워진 것을 보고 부부가 손님들이 신임을 깨닫 고 경외심과 두려움을 느꼈다는 앞의 내용에 역접의 연결사 However(하지만)로 연결되므로, 신들이 친절하게 웃으며 자신 들의 정체를 밝히고 노부부에게 원하는 보상을 말하도록 했다 는 흐름이 되는 identified(밝혔다)가 적절하다. ⓒ 어려운 시절을 겪었지만 여러 해를 함께 행복하게 살았다 는 내용 뒤에 이어지므로, 동일한 맥락으로서, 자신들이 이방 인을 내쫓거나 환대의 대가를 청한 적이 없었다는 겸손하고 정직한 태도를 드러내는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 never에 연결되어 asked(청했다)가 적절하다.

their best season of the year. Baucis even had it in

time. Poor old Baucis wore herself out trying to
catch that goose, but somehow the animal always
got away from her, until the guests made her let it
be, for they had been well served so far. It was a
good meal, and the old couple continued to

week.

Philemon

ⓑ[identified / disguised] themselves as Zeus and

beneath your roof this day when others refused us
shelter. Be sure those shall be punished who would
not help the wandering strangers, but you shall
have whatever reward you choose. Tell us what you

The old man thought for a little while with his
eyes bent on the ground, and then he said: “We
have lived happily together here for many years,
even though the times have been hard. But never
have we turned strangers away or asked for a
reward for entertaining them. To have spoken with
the immortals face to face is a thing few men can
boast of. In this small cottage, humble though it is,
the gods have sat at meal. Neither this place nor
we deserve the honor. If, therefore, you will do
something for us, turn this cottage into a temple
where the gods may always be served and where
we may live out the rest of our days.”
“You have spoken well,” said Hermes, “and you
shall have your wish. Yet is there not anything that
you would desire for yourselves?”
At this, the husband glanced over at old Baucis
with her thin, gray hair and her rough hands. Baucis
said, “We have lived together for many years, and
in all that time never has there been a word of
anger between us. Now, at last, we are growing old
and our long companionship is coming to an end.
Grant us this one request, that when we come to
die, we may perish in the same hour, so that
neither of us would be left without the other.”
She looked at Philemon, and he nodded in approval,
so the old couple turned their eyes on the gods.
“It shall be as you desire,” said Hermes. “Few
would have made such ______________________________.”
Before long, the house became a temple, and the
neighbors, amazed at the change, often came to
worship and left offerings for the gods. For many
years, Baucis and Philemon lived in peace, passing
from old to extreme old age.
choices: a good and moderate request
a meaningless and empty plea
a generous yet unlikely petition
a confusing and ambiguous appeal
an extravagant and unprecedented appeal

body:
Ancient cultures recognized the sun’s power to
sustain life, so it was held in a place of honor in
most mythologies.
The Incas who lived in modern day Peru from the
12th to 16th centuries incorporated the sun in
many aspects of their culture, from holidays to
agriculture. Their sun god, Inti, was one of their
most powerful gods. The Incan royal family was
said to be directly descended from Inti, so his
temples were considered important. The Temple of
the Sun, in the capital city Cuzco, was made of
carved stone and filled with luxurious gold objects.
In Baltic mythology, the sun was represented by
Saule, the mother and ruler of the world, who
determined the well-being of all life on the earth.
(A)황금 스카프와 황금 왕관을 쓴 금발 여인으로 묘사
된 Saule는 바다 끝에 있는 궁전에서 황금 사과 정원
을 가꾸며 살았다. Saule would ride across the sky
in a chariot pulled by two tireless white horses.
Saule was not the only solar god to ride a vehicle
across the sky. The Greek gods Helios and Apollo
were both shown riding chariots through the heavens.
The Egyptian sun god Ra was said to ride in a
solar boat during the day. At night, he sailed
underwater until he returned to the sky in the east.
The sun has been a central figure in some of the
world’s most enduring myths. That is because there
would be no life without that immense force in the
sky.

윗글의 요지로 알맞은 것은?
choices: The sun influenced the daily life and rituals ofancient people.
The sun appeared in stories of gods and heroesin ancient cultures.
The sun, a symbol of energy, featured in manyancient mythologies.
Ancient cultures relied on the sun to regulateseasons and harvests.
The sun, which sustains life, was revered as sacredin ancient mythologies.

Before long, the house became a temple, and the
neighbors, amazed at the (A)[change / consistency],
often came to worship and left offerings for the
gods. For many years, Baucis and Philemon lived in
peace, passing from old to extreme old age. At last,
they were so old and bowed that it seemed they
could only walk if they clung to each other. One
evening, it took them (B)[shorter / longer] than ever
to reach the usual spot they would visit every day
to look at the temple. There they held each other’s
arms, thinking that it was perhaps the last time
their limbs would support them. As they stood,
each one felt the other change and only had time
to turn and say “Farewell,” before they (C)[gained /
lost] their human shapes completely. Now there
stood two tall trees growing closely side by side
with the branches intertwined. They swayed in the
passing breeze as if they nodded and whispered to
each other.

Imagine you are hungry and all you have at home
is a coconut, some rice, and an egg.
(A) If, however, you have memories of your dad
cracking the coconut, and your mom boiling
the rice, your brain can connect the dots and
form a new creative idea.
(B) You boil the rice in coconut water, then fry it
with the egg and add coconut flakes. Voilà!
Enjoy your meal!
(C) If you have no clue and zero creative thoughts,
you’d probably eat the raw egg with unboiled
hard rice while staring at the coconut.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 배가 고픈 상황에서 집에 음식 재료만 있다고 설명한 주어진 문장에 이어, 창의적 생각이 없는 부정적인 상황을 먼저 제시 한 (C), 대조의 however로 연결하여 앞의 상황과 대비시키며 과거의 기억이 있으면 뇌가 여러 정보를 연결하여 창의적 생 각을 떠올릴 수 있다고 설명한 (A), 그 결과로 구체적인 해결 책이 제시되는 (B)로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다.

How do we open ourselves up to new ⓐpossibilities?
One of the ways to do this is to connect things
that look separate. This can be incredibly pleasing
as it helps us to see the world in a different light
and gain a greater ⓑappreciation for the interrelation
of all things. Here are three artists who are willing
to experiment with this approach.
Beyond the Scene
Meet Robin Yayla, a visual storyteller living in Milan,
Italy, who has been delighting his viewers with his
unique artworks on social media. He draws illustrations
on top of photos of landmarks or buildings and
offers whole new ways to see them. To breathe life
into well-known structures around the world, he
often uses iconic pop culture ⓒcharacters.
His unique ⓓtwists sometimes turn what we consider
dull and boring into something delightful. To him, a
bridge is a net, and a road is a bowling lane. After
finding whatever is common in two unrelated things,
he connects them smoothly in his digital drawing.
His work combines his ⓔpassion for traveling and
drawing. Exploring new places and learning about
new cultures inspire his artistic mind to come up
with new ideas for his art. Many of his digital
illustrations (A)__________________________________________
______________ that you would like to see again. For
example, he added images of ice cream cones onto
the scenic photo of St. Basil’s Cathedral in Moscow,
the capital of Russia. The Leaning Tower of Pisa,
one of the most remarkable architectural structures
in Italy, appeared to be a camera lens to him.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: something that may happen or may be true
ⓑ: understanding of the importance or meaningof something
ⓒ: the particular combination of qualities thatmakes someone a particular type of person
ⓓ: an unexpected change or development
ⓔ: a strong enthusiasm or interest in something
solution: characters는 지문에서 상징적인 대중문화 속 ‘인물들’의 의미 로 쓰였으므로, ‘사람의 성격[기질]’을 나타내는 ❸ ‘누군가를 특정 유형의 사람으로 만드는 특별한 성향의 조합’은 알맞지 않다. ⓒ character (→ a person in a story, film, play, etc. 이야기, 영화, 연극 등에 등장하는 인물)

body:
When we look at shadows of objects in real life,
most of us think nothing of them. Belgian artist
and film-maker Vincent Bal, however, turns them
into art forms. He lets his creativity ⓐflow to make
beautiful and meaningful scenes with shadows.
His playful shadow art illustrations are made by
adding his own doodles to shadows cast from
everyday objects, like a flower or a glass. In one
image, the shadow from a key is reinterpreted as a
DJ wearing headphones. In another, a potato peeler
creates the perfectly shaped frame for a piano. In
his art, the shadow from a glass becomes a pool.
He uses a very simple process to draw his
pictures. To start the process, all he needs to do ⓑis
prepare a plain object, a piece of paper, and a
light. Then he puts the object on the paper and
turns on the light. He just starts moving the light
around and places the object in different positions.
He keeps a very open mind and tries not to have
an idea in advance about ⓒwhat the result should
be.
“If I try to shape a shadow into a certain form, it
always feels a bit (A)___________. If nothing comes, I
take another object, and then I just start playing
around with it until suddenly I see something. In
this way, I can create ⓓwhatever I want,” he says.
His free artistic interpretation of shadows means
that the possibilities for creating new doodles are
(B)____________.
In fact, it was by accident ⓔthat he started
making his art pieces. While he was working on a
new script, he suddenly noticed how the shadow of
a cup on his desk looked like a little elephant. He
completed the image with a few lines, took a
picture and shared it on the Internet. The reactions
were so positive that he challenged himself to make
one shadow image every day.

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

(A)
(B)
choices: forcedendless
controlledrestricted
liberatedcountless
stressedlimited
freelimitless
solution: (A) 결과가 어떠해야 한다는 생각을 미리 하지 않으려 노력하 며, 무언가가 보일 때까지 이리저리 만지작거리기 시작한다고 언급되었으므로, 그림자를 특정한 형태로 만들려고 하다 보면 늘 ‘억지스러운(forced)' 느낌이 든다는 흐름이 알맞다. (B) 무언가가 보일 때까지 이리저리 만지작거리기 시작하면 그 가 원하는 것은 무엇이든 만들어 낼 수 있다고 언급하고 있으 므로, 그의 자유로운 예술적 해석은 새로운 낙서를 만들 가능 성이 '무한하(endless, countless, limitless)'다는 것을 뜻한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

I became a book artist almost by accident. After
ⓐgraduating in 2003, I traveled to Thailand. At that
time, I didn’t think about working with books.
ⓑShop in Bangkok, I came across a used book
with beautiful notes written in it. That got me
interested in the way paper was used in art. Soon
after I returned to the UK, my father passed away.
Feeling sad, I found myself picking up the Graham
Greene classic I had brought back from my trip and
ⓒcutting paper moths out of the pages. I then
hung them over the open book. Since then, I have
created sculptures out of books.
I always read the story first to get inspiration, and
everything for the sculpture is made from the
pages
within
that
book;
some
don’t
have
illustrations, so I take inspiration from the title and
the text. I am also drawn toward fairy tales,
especially Hans Christian Andersen’s; his tales are
quite magical, but there’s also a sadness as they
don’t always have a happy ending.
For me, books are not only sources of ideas and
associations, but also objects of great beauty ⓓto
be cut up and rearranged. I use very simple tools:
a sharp knife, a bit of glue, and some wire. Utilizing
the open book as my base, I cut its pages, glue
them, gently ⓔpull up them, and support them with
wire. Through these processes, I construct physical
representations of the narratives and the characters.

Surprising Connection

(A)[fused / divided] in one painting. They usually
depict landscapes and objects that ⓐseem to
change from one thing to another.
When you look at the top right corner of the
painting above, you can see a kid jumping on his
bed. However, as you move your eyes across, the
bedcovers change into fields, ⓑwhich a girl now
appears to be flying. This is how the visual illusion
is created: an object is gradually changed through a
series of similar shapes into something entirely
(B)[identical / different] in a single scene. At the
same time, two different parts of the same scene
are constructed at different scales. The result is an
unexpected and seemingly impossible whole.
This kind of illusion has a fun way of ⓒtwisting
your perception. It makes you question what is real.
Most of his incredible paintings have a(n) (C)[clear /
unclear] boundary between the multiple stories they
tell, which forces the viewer ⓓto jump back and
forth between them. ⓔTrace the transitions, you get

Weidensaul: To find their routes, the bar-tailed
godwits probably rely on the sun and stars
among other things. Some experts believe that
they may be able to sense the earth’s magnetic
field lines, too. You may also wonder how, if
ever, they sleep while flying over a vast ocean.
It turns out that migratory birds use an
approach called “half-brain sleep.” This is how it
works. Only the left half of the brain sleeps for
a couple of seconds, then only the right half
for the next couple of seconds, and then this
process repeats over and over again. Isn’t it
amazing? Actually, some sea mammals like
dolphins can do that, too, because they have
to keep breathing consciously.

to have such an ability?

undergo the same journey back to Alaska. They

(A)[flied / flying] up to 30,000 km every year. By

than two weeks and make another flight of
