(B) 멸종 위기에 처한 햄스터를 묘지에서 볼 수 있다고 언급했으 며, 햄스터가 견과류와 꽃뿐만 아니라 좋은 지방 공급원으로서 양 초 왁스를 먹는 데도 적응했다고 설명하고 있으므로, 묘지에서 양 초 왁스를 쉽게 찾을 수 있다는 흐름이 되는 easy(쉬운)가 알맞다. (C) 도시가 실제로 야생 동물을 보호하는 섬이 될 수 있다는 내용이 뒤에 이어지므로, 양보의 전치사 Despite(~에도 불구하 고)에 연결된 내용으로서, 도시 지역들이 일반적으로 야생 동 물에게 부정적인 영향을 미친다는 대조적인 흐름이 되는 negative(부정적인)가 알맞다.

body:
Today, I’m looking for a tiny animal that’s hiding
in one of Europe’s most beautiful capital cities,
Vienna. Now it’s home to nearly 2 million people,
but 50% of the city is green space. What I’m
looking for is probably one of Europe’s most
critically endangered mammals.
Now, I’ve come really early to a graveyard to try to
see some hamsters because this is one of the
(A)[best / worst] times of day to see them. At this
time of the day, there’s nobody around so they don’t
have to avoid people while looking for food. These
little ones have been in the area for decades, but
now live among the dead because development has
robbed them of the green fields they used to inhabit.
Look! I just found one over there. See how it is
trying to stuff its cheeks full? Hamsters can pack a
quarter of their body weight inside their cheeks,
which
helps
them
get
through
the
winter.
Surprisingly, they not only feed on nuts and
flowers, but have also adapted to eating candle
wax, which is a good source of fat and is (B)[easy /
hard] to find in graveyards.
Even though the hamsters here have adapted to
the noises of the city, they still keep a watchful
eye, as predators are never too far away. ⓐ그들은
재빨리 굴속으로 도망쳐야 할 수도 있는데, 그것은 땅
속으로 뻗어 있는 복잡한 구조물입니다. Despite
urban
areas
generally
having
a
(C)[positive
/
negative] effect on wildlife, cities can actually
provide islands of protection for it.

윗글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
choices: What percentage of the total area of Vienna iscomposed of green space?
What caused the hamsters to move their habitatinto the graveyard?
How much food can a hamster store in itscheeks relative to its weight?
What unusual source of fat have these hamstersadapted to eating in the city?
What are the specific types of predators thatthreaten hamsters in Vienna?
solution: 빈의 묘지에 사는 햄스터들은 도시의 소음에 적응했지만 포식 동물이 멀리 떨어져 있지 않기 때문에 여전히 주의 깊게 지켜 본다고 했을 뿐, 어떤 포식자들이 그들 근처에 있는지에 대한 언급은 없으므로, ❺ ‘빈에서 햄스터들을 위협하는 포식자들의 구체적인 종류는 무엇인가?’에는 답할 수 없다. 천재(강상구) 4과 정답 본 콘텐츠는 해당 출판사로부터 교과서 라이센스를 획득하여 이그잼포유에서 제작하였습니다. 본 콘텐츠에 대한 저작권은 이그잼포유가 소유하고 있으며, 콘텐츠의 전부 또는 일부를 무단 전재하거나 배포하는 것은 저작권법에 의한 법적 책임 을 물을 수 있습니다. 본 콘텐츠의 레이아웃 및 편집에 대한 저작권 침해 행위 또한 금지하고 있습니다. 영어I 천재(강상구) 4과 예상문제 1회 - 객관식(선다형) 1. ③ 2. ④ 3. ④ 4. ⑤ 5. ④ 6. 주관식 7. ④ 8. ③ 9. ① 10. ③ 11. ① 12. 주관식 13. 주관식 14. ⑤ 15. ⑤ 16. ④ 17. ⑤ 18. ③ 19. 주관식 20. ⑤ 정답 및 해설 ┃1회┃ 1) ③: 밑줄 친 (A) ‘that’s a relief’는 ‘다행이다’라는 뜻으로, 멸종 위기에 처해 있던 유라시아 수달이 현재는 개체 수가 회 복되고 있다는 소녀의 말을 듣고 다행이라는 뜻의 안도 감을 나타내는 의미로 쓰였으므로, 유감을 나타내는 ③ ‘that’s too bad(안됐다)’와는 바꿔 쓸 수 없다. 참고로, ‘That’s a relief.’는 ‘I’m relieved.(나는 안심이 된다.)’, ‘What a relief!(정말 다행이다!)’, ‘I’m glad to hear that. (나는 그 말을 들으니 기쁘다.)’ ‘That’s a weight off my mind.(안심이다.)’ 등으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다. 오답 ① 나는 안심이 돼 ② 정말 다행이야 ④ 나는 그 말을 들으니 기뻐 ⑤ 안심이야 2) ④: 예전에는 값비싼 모피와 가죽 때문에 유라시아 수달들이 사냥을 당해서 멸종 위기에 처했으며, 요즘에는 인간 활 동 때문에 서식지가 사라지는 것이 더 큰 위협이라고 했 으므로, ④ ‘과거 유라시아 수달들의 멸종 위기에 대한 주요 원인은 자연의 포식자들이었다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다. 오답 ① 소녀는 그 다큐멘터리에서 특히 유라시아 수달들에 관한 부분에 깊은 인상을 받았다. ② 유라시아 수달들은 장난기가 많고 물고기를 잡는 데 능숙한 것으로 알려져 있다. ③ 유라시아 수달들은 14미터 깊이까지 잠수할 수 있다. ⑤ 보존 노력들 덕분에 현재 유라시아 수달들의 수가 증 가하고 있다. 3) ④: Scott Weidensaul이 지난 수십 년간 철새를 연구해 왔다 고 했으므로, ④ ‘Scott Weidensaul은 최근에 철새들을 연구하는 것에 대한 경력을 시작했다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다. 오답 ① 상당한 수의 새들이 밤 동안에 이동한다. ② 그 이동은 막대한 거리를 이동하는 수십억 마리의 새 들을 포함한다. ③ Scott Weidensaul은 그의 전문 지식을 나누기 위해 Jo’s Tea Time에 손님으로 초대되었다. ⑤ Scott Weidensaul은 철새라는 주제에 관해 글을 써왔다. 4) ⑤: 밤에 우리의 머리 바로 위로 대규모 이동이 일어날 때가 있다는 것을 아는지 물으며, 수십억 마리의 새들이 수천 킬로미터까지 여행하는 철새 이동의 규모가 경외감을 불 러일으킨다고 언급한 후, 오랫동안 철새를 연구하고 철 새에 관한 책을 써온 동물학자이자 작가인 Scott Weidensaul의 지식을 나누고자 그를 소개하고 있으므로, 이어질 내용으로 ⑤ ‘수많은 새들이 왜 이동하는지, 그리 고 어떻게 그렇게 먼 거리들을 여행하는지에 대한 설명’ 이 알맞다. 오답 ① 철새들이 국경을 넘어 어떻게 질병들을 퍼뜨리는지에 대한 분석 ② Weidensaul 씨에 의해 쓰인 베스트셀러 도서들에 대 한 소개 ③ 청취자들을 위한 동물학자로서의 경력을 시작하는 방 법에 대한 일련의 조언들 ④ 왜 새들이 다른 동물들보다 더 나은 반려동물이 되는 지에 대한 논의 5) ④: ⓓ visibly → visible (동사 make와 목적어인 대명사 everything 에 이어져 ‘make+목적어+목적격보어’(~을 …하게 만들다) 의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리로, 보어 자리에 는 부사가 쓰일 수 없으므로 형용사인 visible로 고친다.) 오답 ⓒ be동사인 is의 보어 자리에서 결과를 나타내는 완전한 절(it’s hard ~ happening)을 이끌어야 하므로, 선행사 the reason이 생략된 이유의 관계부사 why는 알맞다. ⓔ 과거시제로 쓰인 동사 found와 목적어 the bar-tailed godwits에 이어져 ‘find+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사구)(~ 를 …하다고 생각하다)’를 이루어야 하므로 to부정사인 to be는 알맞다. 6) They migrate at night because the night sky is cooler, the air calmer : • 주절인 ‘They migrate at night’에 이어 <보기>의 because를 사용해 이유를 나타내는 부사절을 연결한다. • 부사절의 주어 the night sky와 be동사 is에 이어지는 주격보어 자리에 형용사 cool(시원한)을 비교급인 cooler로 변형하여 쓴다. • 완전한 절 the night sky is cooler에 등위접속사 and로 이어지는 절의 주어로 the air를 쓰고, <조건>에 따라 반 복되는 be동사 is를 생략한 뒤, 보어 자리에 calm의 비교 급 calmer를 쓴다. 영어I 천재(강상구) 4과 예상문제 1회 - 주관식(서답형) 6. (1) They may need to quickly escape back down (2) which are complex structures stretching under the ground 7) ④: 매년 봄과 가을에 수억에서 수십억 마리에 달하는 철새 가 밤에 이동한다고 했으므로, 밤하늘을 걷어 내고 모든 것을 볼 수 있게 만든다면, 엄청난 수의 새들이 날아가 는 광경을 목격할 수 있을 것이라는 흐름이 되는 ④ ‘지 구상에서 가장 크고 멋진 자연의 장관이다’가 알맞다. 오답 ① 새들이 작은 무리들로 이동하는 것을 선호함을 증명 하다 ② 우리의 최선의 노력들에도 불구하고 숨겨진 미스터리 로 남다 ③ 사람들이 거의 알아채지 못할 미묘한 변화이다 ⑤ 계절적인 기온 변화들의 단순한 결과이다 8) ③: 주어진 문장은 ‘실제로 저는 동아시아-대양주 철새 이동 경로에 위치한 국가들로 이루어진 국제 조직과 함께 일 하고 있습니다.’라는 뜻으로, 황해를 보존하는 더 큰 차 원의 노력으로서 여러 나라를 거쳐 여행하는 철새의 보 호를 위해 국제적인 협력이 꼭 필요하다는 주어진 문장 에 상응하는 내용 뒤이자, Weidensaul과 협력하는 국제 조직을 we로 받아, 우리의 국제적인 협력의 결과로 멸종 위기에 처한 저어새를 성공적으로 되살릴 수 있었다는 내용 앞인 (C)에 들어가야 한다. 9) ①: 큰뒷부리도요와 같은 철새들이 넓은 바다 위를 나는 동 안 잠을 자는 방법으로, 몇 초 동안 두뇌의 좌반구만 잠 을 자다가 다음 몇 초는 우반구만 잠을 자는 ‘반뇌수면’ 을 사용하고, 돌고래와 같은 일부 해양 포유동물들 또한 이런 능력이 있다는 설명에 대한 반응으로 이어져야 하 며, 뒤에 그런 능력을 갖는 걸 마다할 사람이 없을 것이 라고 덧붙이고 있으므로, 그것이 놀라운 능력이라는 흐 름이 되는 ① ‘기막힌 재주’가 알맞다. 오답 ② 위험한 행동 ③ 단순한 과업 ④ 치명적인 실수 ⑤ 흔한 습관 10) ③: 큰뒷부리도요가 길을 찾기 위해 해와 별에 의존하거나 지구의 자기력선을 감지할 것이라고 했으며, 철새들이 두뇌의 양쪽 부분을 번갈아 이용하여 잠을 자는 ‘반뇌 수면’을 통해 날아가는 중에도 잠을 잘 수 있다고 설명 하므로, 글의 주제로 ③ ‘철새들이 어떻게 길을 찾고 비 행 중에 잠을 자는지’가 알맞다. 오답 ① 조류의 비행에 대한 자기장 간섭의 위험성들 ② 돌고래들이 서로 의사소통하는 방법에 대한 비밀 ④ 태평양 전역에 걸친 다양한 종의 철새들 ⑤ 해양 포유동물들의 자연 서식지들을 보존하는 것의 중요성 11) ①: ⓐ what → that[which] 또는 what 삭제 (타동사로 쓰인 do의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(they can’t do at other times of the year)을 이끌어 선행사인 things를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로, 선행사를 포함 하고 불완전한 절을 이끄는 관계대명사 what을 목적격 관계대명사인 that이나 which로 고치거나, 목적격 관계 대명사는 생략할 수 있으므로 what을 삭제한다.) *ⓐ는 원래 지문에서 that이었음 오답 ⓓ By the time(~할 때쯤)이 이끄는 부사구가 나타내는 미래 시점까지 증가한 상태일 것이라는 의미로, 추측의 조동사 may 뒤에 완료를 나타내는 have p.p.를 사용한 have increased는 알맞다. 12) (A) birds in migratory condition (B) Some bar-tailed godwits (C) their digestive organs : (A) they는 앞 문장에 언급된 birds in migratory condition (이동을 하는 상태의 새들)을 가리킨다. (B) They는 앞 문장에 언급된 Some bar-tailed godwits(몇 몇 큰뒷부리도요들)를 가리킨다. (C) these는 앞서 언급된 their digestive organs(그것들의 소화 기관들)를 가리킨다. 13) (1) ⓓ consisted → consisting (2) ⓔ to see → see : ⓓ 앞에 문장의 동사(am working)가 있으므로 흐름상 명 사구 an international organization(국제 조직)을 수식하는 분사(구)를 이루는 분사가 쓰이는 것은 알맞으나, ‘이루어 지다’라는 뜻의 자동사 consist는 수동태나 수동을 나타내 는 과거분사로 쓰이지 않으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분 사 consisting으로 고친다. ⓔ 동사 let과 목적어인 대명사 us에 이어져 ‘let+목적어+ 목적격보어’(~가 …하게 하다)의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적 격보어 자리로, 목적어인 us(우리)가 ‘보는’ 주체이며, 사역 동사 let의 목적어와 목적격보어가 능동 관계이면 목적격 보어로 동사원형이 쓰이므로, 동사원형인 see로 고친다. 오답 ⓐ 앞의 추상명사 idea의 구체적 내용을 설명하는 완전한 절(the Yellow Sea has such importance)을 연결하고 있으 므로 동격 접속사 that은 알맞다. 14) ⑤: Weidensaul과 한 조직의 국제적인 협력의 결과로 멸종 위기에 처한 저어새를 성공적으로 되살릴 수 있었다고 했으므로, ⑤ ‘국제적인 협력에도 불구하고, 저어새의 개체 수를 회복시키려는 시도는 성공하지 못했다.’는 일 치하지 않는 내용이다. 오답 ① 황해는 철새들에게 중요한 집합지의 역할을 한다. ② 해변가를 청소하는 것과 같은 개인적인 행동들은 새 들을 보호하는 데 도움이 될 수 있다. ③ 철새들을 보호하는 것은 서로 다른 국가들 간의 협 력을 필요로 한다. ④ Weidensaul 씨는 동아시아-대양주 철새 이동 경로 를 따라 위치한 국가들의 국제 집단과 협력하고 있다. 15) ⑤: 길을 찾기 위해 큰뒷부리도요는 아마 무엇보다 해와 별 에 의존할 것이라는 주어진 글에 이어, 큰뒷부리도요새 들을 they로 받아 이들이 길을 찾는 다른 방법으로서, 어떤 전문가들은 그 새들이 지구의 자기력선을 감지할 수 있으리라 생각한다는 내용과, 그들이 바다 위를 날 며 잠을 잔다면 어떻게 그렇게 하는지 궁금할 것이라는 (C), (C)의 마지막 문장에 대한 답변으로서, 철새가 ‘반 뇌수면’이라고 부르는 방법을 사용하는 것으로 드러났 다는 내용과, ‘반뇌수면’에 대한 설명으로 몇 초 동안 두뇌의 좌반구만 잠을 자다가 다음 몇 초는 우반구만 잠을 자고 이 과정을 반복한다는 (B), (C)의 마지막 문 장에 언급된 새의 능력에 대해 놀랍지 않냐고 물은 뒤, ‘반뇌수면’을 that으로 받아 실제로 돌고래와 같은 해양 포유동물들도 의식적으로 숨을 계속 쉬기 위해 그것을 할 수 있다고 설명하는 (A)의 흐름이 자연스럽다. 16) ④: ⓓ tiny(아주 작은) → enormous(방대한) 본문변형 Then what happens after they arrive there? → Then what happens after the bar-tailed godwits arrive in New Zealand? 17) ⑤: (A) 앞의 완전한 절(They ~ years)에 접속사 없이 쉼표 로만 연결되므로 분사구문을 이끄는 분사 자리이며, 주 절의 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어인 they(=the bar-tailed godwits(큰뒷부리도요들))가 ‘나는’ 주체이므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 flying이 알맞다. (B) 주어부 ‘these ~ tidal mud’에 이어진 문장의 동사 자리로, 주어부의 핵심 단어인 복수명사 stretches에 수 일치한 복수동사 look이 알맞다. (C) ‘~들 중의 하나’라는 뜻을 나타내는 ‘one of+정관사 (the)+복수명사(구)’를 이루어야 하므로, 복수명사와 함 께 쓰이는 few에 복수명사 places가 이어진 few places 가 알맞다. 18) ③: (A) 이른 시간대에는 묘지 주변에 사람이 없기 때문에 햄스터들이 먹이를 찾는 동안 사람을 피할 필요가 없 다는 내용이 이어지므로, 지금이 하루 중 햄스터를 보 기 가장 좋은 시간대 중 하나라는 흐름이 되는 best(가 장 좋은)가 알맞다. worst 가장 나쁜 (B) 멸종 위기에 처한 햄스터를 묘지에서 볼 수 있다고 언급했으며, 햄스터가 견과류와 꽃뿐만 아니라 좋은 지 방 공급원으로서 양초 왁스를 먹는 데도 적응했다고 설명하고 있으므로, 묘지에서 양초 왁스를 쉽게 찾을 수 있다는 흐름이 되는 easy(쉬운)가 알맞다. hard 힘든 (C) 도시가 실제로 야생 동물을 보호하는 섬이 될 수 있다는 내용이 뒤에 이어지므로, 양보의 전치사 Despite(~에도 불구하고)에 연결된 내용으로서, 도시 지역들이 일반적으로 야생 동물에게 부정적인 영향을 미친다는 대조적인 흐름이 되는 negative(부정적인)가 알맞다. positive 긍정적인 19) (1) They may need to quickly escape back down (2) which are complex structures stretching under the ground : (1) 조동사 may와 동사원형 need를 쓴 뒤, ‘~해야 한다’라 는 뜻의 ‘need+to부정사’를 사용하여 to부정사구를 연결하 되, <조건>에 따라 부사의 동사 수식을 강조하기 위해 쓰 이는 ‘to+부사+동사원형’ 구조의 분리부정사를 사용하여 부사 quickly(재빨리)가 to와 동사원형 escape 사이에 오게 한다. (2) • 쉼표 뒤에 앞의 명사구 their holes를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 쓰되, <조건>에 따라 계속적 용법의 주격 관 계대명사로 which를 쓰고 뒤에 주어가 없는 불완전한 절 을 연결한다. 선행사 their holes가 복수명사구이므로 which가 이끄는 절의 동사 자리에 복수동사 are를 써서 수 일치 시키고, 보어로 명사구 complex structures를 쓴다. • 분사(구)를 사용하라는 <조건>에 따라 명사구 complex structures(복잡한 구조물들)를 수식하는 분사구를 쓰되, 수 식을 받는 명사구가 ‘뻗어 있는’ 주체이므로, 능동의 의미 를 지닌 현재분사 stretching이 분사구를 이끌도록 한다. 20) ⑤: 빈의 묘지에 사는 햄스터들은 도시의 소음에 적응했지 만 포식 동물이 멀리 떨어져 있지 않기 때문에 여전히 주의 깊게 지켜본다고 했을 뿐, 어떤 포식자들이 그들 근처에 있는지에 대한 언급은 없으므로, ⑤ ‘빈에서 햄 스터들을 위협하는 포식자들의 구체적인 종류는 무엇 인가?’에는 답할 수 없다. 오답 ① 빈의 전체 지역 중 몇 퍼센트가 녹지 공간으로 구 성되어 있는가? (→50%) ② 무엇이 햄스터들로 하여금 그들의 서식지를 묘지로 옮기게 만들었는가? (→개발) ③ 햄스터는 자신의 몸무게와 비교했을 때 얼마나 많 은 음식을 볼에 저장할 수 있는가? (→4분의 1) ④ 도시에서 이 햄스터들은 어떤 독특한 지방 공급원 을 먹도록 적응하였는가? (→양초 왁스)

W: Hello, everyone. Today, I’ll talk about the
importance of imagination in producing effective
advertisements.
(A) So, this advertisement successfully captures people’s
attention and helps them understand the problem
the African penguins are facing. Please keep in
mind that using your imagination is essential in
creating great advertisements.
(B) The advertisement shown in this poster is an
excellent illustration of how imagination can be
used to raise awareness of critical issues.
(C) A striking pattern of black and white penguins
creates a powerful visual presentation of the
rapidly declining African penguin population,
and most of all, the use of a clever visual trick
highlights the problem.

위 주어진 담화에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 광고 제작에서 상상력의 중요성을 설명하는 담화로, 상상력이 중요한 문제에 대한 인식을 높이는 데 활용될 수 있음을 포스 터 광고 사례로 제시하는 (B), 흑백 펭귄의 눈에 띄는 패턴을 언급하며 그 효과를 구체적으로 설명하고 있는 (C), So로 시작 하여 해당 광고가 주의를 끌고 문제를 이해하게 한다고 결론 지은 뒤, 상상력이 훌륭한 광고를 만드는 데 필수적임을 강조 하는 (A)의 순서로 이어져야 한다.

다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?

Surprising Connection
Paintings of Rob Gonsalves, a Canadian magic
realist artist, combine two different points of view.
They give the viewer the visual illusion that they
are looking at two unrelated realities flawlessly
fused
in
one
painting.
They
usually
depict
landscapes and objects that seem to change from
one thing to another.
When you look at the top right corner of the
painting above, you can see a kid jumping on his
bed. However, as you move your eyes across, the
bedcovers change into fields, which a girl now
appears to be flying over. This is how the visual
illusion is created: an object is gradually changed
through a series of similar shapes into something
entirely different in a single scene. At the same
time, two different parts of the same scene are
constructed at different scales. The result is an
unexpected and seemingly impossible whole.
This kind of illusion has a fun way of twisting your
perception. It makes you question what is real.
Most of his incredible paintings have an unclear
boundary between the multiple stories they tell,
which forces the viewer to jump back and forth
between them. Tracing the transitions, you get that
delightful “Ah-ha!” feeling as you try to decide
exactly where one world transforms into another.
choices: How does Rob Gonsalves create a visual illusionin his paintings?
What happens to the bedcovers as the viewermoves their eyes across the painting?
How long does Rob Gonsalves usually take tocomplete one painting?
What effect do the unclear boundaries betweenmultiple stories have on the viewer?
When does the viewer feel an “Ah-ha!” momentwhile looking at the painting?
solution: Rob Gonsalves의 작품 제작 시간에 대한 정보는 언급된 바가 없으므로, ❸ ‘Rob Gonsalves는 보통 한 점의 그림을 완성하는 데 얼마나 걸리는가?는 답할 수 없는 질문이다. 천재(강상구) 2과

How do we open ourselves up to new possibilities?
One of the ways to do this is to connect things
that look separate. This can be incredibly ⓐpleased
as it helps us to see the world in a different light

body:
Surprising Connection
Paintings of Rob Gonsalves, a Canadian magic
realist artist, combine two different points of view.
They give the viewer the visual illusion that they
are looking at ⓐ_______________________________________
__________________ They usually depict landscapes and
objects that seem to change from one thing to
another.
When you look at the top right corner of the
painting above, you can see a kid jumping on his
bed. However, as you move your eyes across, the
bedcovers change into fields, which a girl now
appears to be flying over. This is (A)[how / what]
the visual illusion is created: an object is gradually
changed through a series of similar shapes into
something entirely different in a single scene. At
the same time, two different parts of the same
scene are constructed at different scales. The result
is an unexpected and seemingly impossible whole.
This kind of illusion has a fun way of twisting your
perception. It makes you question what is real.
Most of his incredible paintings have an unclear
boundary between the multiple stories they tell,
which (B)[force / forces] the viewer to jump back
and forth between them. (C)[Tracing / Traced] the
transitions, you get that delightful “Ah-ha!” feeling
as you try to decide exactly where one world
transforms into another.

윗글의 빈칸 ⓐ에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: a single object shown repeatedly from differentangles
two unrelated realities flawlessly fused in onepainting
ordinary scenes transformed by advanced artistictechniques
two familiar landscapes realistically painted ingreat detail
different stories clearly separated within thesame painting
solution: Rob Gonsalves의 그림은 두 가지 다른 관점을 결합하여, 침대 보가 들판으로 변하는 것처럼 풍경이나 사물이 다른 것으로 점진적으로 바뀌는 착시를 만들어 내기에, 그 결과가 예상치 못하고 겉보기에는 불가능해 보이는 완전체라고 언급하고 있 으므로, 우리가 보는 시각적 착시로, 빈칸에는 ❷ ‘하나의 그림 에 완벽하게 융합된 서로 관련이 없는 두 현실’이 들어가는 것 이 알맞다.

When we look at shadows of objects in real life,
most of us think nothing of them. Belgian artist
and film-maker Vincent Bal, however, turns them
into art forms. (A) He lets his creativity flow to
make
beautiful
and
meaningful
scenes
with
shadows. (B)
His playful shadow art illustrations are made by
adding his own doodles to shadows cast from
everyday objects, like a flower or a glass. (C) In
another, a potato peeler creates the perfectly
shaped frame for a piano. (D) In his art, the
shadow from a glass becomes a pool. (E)
He uses a very ㉠[simple / complex] process to
draw his pictures. To start the process, all he needs
to do is prepare a plain object, a piece of paper,
and a light. Then he puts the object on the paper
and turns on the light. He just starts moving the
light around and places the object in different
positions. He keeps a very open mind and tries not
to have an idea in advance about what the result
should be.
“If I try to shape a shadow into a certain form, it
always feels a bit forced. If nothing comes, I take
another object, and then I just start playing around
with it until suddenly I see something. In this way, I
can create whatever I want,” he says. His ㉡[free /
controlled] artistic interpretation of shadows means
that the possibilities for creating new doodles are
endless.
In fact, it was ㉢[by accident / on purpose] that
he started making his art pieces. While he was
working on a new script, he suddenly noticed how
the shadow of a cup on his desk looked like a
little elephant. He completed the image with a few
lines, took a picture and shared it on the Internet.
ⓐ반응이 너무 긍정적이어서 그는 매일 하나의 그림자
그림을 만드는 데 도전했다.
Art can inspire you to see the world from a new
angle. Connecting ideas that at first glance appear
unrelated is a powerful tool for exploring the
beauty of the world around us. To make such
connections, all you need is your imaginative power.

윗글의 괄호 ㉠, ㉡, ㉢에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

㉠
㉡
㉢
choices: simplefreeby accident
simplecontrolledby accident
complexcontrolledon purpose
simplefreeon purpose
complexfreeby accident
solution: ㉠ 과정을 시작하기 위해, 그가 할 일은 평범한 물건, 종이 한 장, 그리고 조명을 준비하는 것뿐이라는 내용이 이어지므로, 그림을 그리는 데 매우 '간단한(simple)' 과정을 사용한다는 흐 름이 알맞다. ㉡ 그림자를 특정한 형태로 만들려고 하거나 미리 정해두지 않고 무언가가 보일 때까지 이리저리 만지작거린다는 앞 내용 으로 보아 그는 그림자에 대해 ‘자유로운(free)' 예술적 해석을 갖고 있다는 흐름이 알맞다. ㉢ 새로운 대본 작업을 하던 중, 그는 문득 책상 위에 놓인 컵 의 그림자가 작은 코끼리처럼 보인다는 것을 깨닫고 그 위에 선을 몇 개 더해 그린 그림이 인터넷 상에서 긍정적인 반응을 얻자 매일 그리기 시작한 것이 그의 예술 작품 활동의 계기가 되었으므로 ’우연히(by accident)'가 알맞다.

body:
-Su Blackwell
I became a book artist almost by accident. After
graduating in 2003, I traveled to Thailand. At that
time, I didn’t think about working with books.
Shopping in Bangkok, I came across a used book
with beautiful notes ⓐwritten in it. That got me
interested in the way paper was used in art. Soon
after I returned to the UK, my father passed away.
㉠슬픔을 느끼며, 나는 여행에서 돌아올 때 가져온
Graham Greene의 고전을 집어 들어 페이지들에서 종이
나방을 오려 내고 있는 나를 발견했다. I then hung
them over the open book. Since then, I ⓑhave
created sculptures out of books.
I always read the story first ⓒto get inspiration,
and everything for the sculpture is made from the
pages
within
that
book;
some
don’t
have
illustrations, so I take inspiration from the title and
the text. I am also drawn toward fairy tales,
especially Hans Christian Andersen’s; his tales are
quite magical, but there’s also a sadness as they
don’t always have a happy ending.
For me, books are not only sources of ideas and
associations, but also objects of great beauty to be
cut up and ⓓrearrange. I use very simple tools: a
sharp knife, a bit of glue, and some wire. ⓔUtilizing
the open book as my base, I cut its pages, glue
them, gently pull them up, and support them with
wire. Through these processes, I construct physical
representations of the narratives and the characters.

How do we open ourselves up to new possibilities?
One of the ways to do this is to ⓐisolate things
that look separate. This can be incredibly pleasing
as it helps us to see the world in a different light
and gain a greater appreciation for the interrelation
of all things. Here are three artists who are willing
to experiment with this approach.
Beyond the Scene
Meet Robin Yayla, a visual storyteller living in
Milan, Italy, who has been delighting his viewers
with his unique artworks on social media. He draws
illustrations on ⓑtop of photos of landmarks or
buildings and offers whole new ways to see them.
To breathe life into well-known structures around the
world, he often uses iconic pop culture characters.
His unique ⓒtwists sometimes turn what we
consider dull and boring into something delightful.
To him, a bridge is a net, and a road is a bowling
lane. After finding whatever is common in two
unrelated things, he connects them smoothly in his
digital drawing.
His work combines his ⓓpassion for traveling and
drawing. Exploring new places and learning about
new cultures inspire his artistic mind to come up
with new ideas for his art. Many of his digital
illustrations ⓔtransform the most historic buildings
of the world into new objects that you would like
to see again. For example, he added images of ice
cream cones onto the scenic photo of St. Basil’s
Cathedral in Moscow, the capital of Russia. The
Leaning Tower of Pisa, one of the most remarkable
architectural structures in Italy, appeared to be a
camera lens to him.

body:
Part 2 My Two-week Detox
Day 1
So it was time to pull the plug.
I grabbed my phone. I swiped it open and stared
at the social media icons dotting the screen. I
removed the apps from my phone. Then I moved
to my notebook computer. I logged out of all of
the social media sites. I felt an immediate sense of
relief.
But soon after, I got restless. I don’t remember
how long it was, but I stared at my phone screen
in complete confusion for quite a while. I called
Jamie, and we chatted for about an hour. But
there’s only so much you can do over a voice call.
We decided to meet later in the afternoon for a
bike ride.
What else can I do on my phone? I lay on my
bed even though I wasn’t sleepy. I stayed there
until I went out to meet Jamie. Throughout the
day, it felt like things slowed down considerably.
What a long day!

Volunteering has a great deal of benefits. ㉠당신은
누군가의 삶에 긍정적인 영향을 미칠 뿐만 아니라, 당
신의 경력에 귀중한 기술들도 습득할 수 있다. It even
reduces stress and anxiety. With busy schedules, it
can be hard to find the time to commit to
volunteer work. These days, however, you can make
a huge difference in the lives of others from your
own home by virtually volunteering. Here are a few
ways to virtually volunteer.
First, you could be a part of the effort to lend
support
to
senior
citizens
who
struggle
with
loneliness. (A) Typically, volunteer “phone friends”
make regular calls to chat and check in with these
people. (B) Second, you can help people with low or
no vision with their everyday tasks. (C) Through a
live video call, you can offer visual assistance to
those who need it with tasks such as reading “use
by” dates and instructions on food packages, which
helps them to lead more independent lives. (D) Also,
specialized technology, such as screen readers and
voice-controlled
devices, helps visually impaired
people. (E) Finally, if you have an interest in wildlife
and its conservation, you can help with animal
monitoring work by watching live videos of animal
habitats around the world. Monitoring these animals
helps protect wildlife and develop methods of
conserving them.
Helping others and giving back to the community
can be very rewarding. It can make your day more
meaningful and productive. It is also a great way to
connect with new people and cultures. For those
who believe in karma, if you do good things for
others, good things will happen to you!

Part 1 FOMO (Fear of Missing Out)
“Selena. SELENA!”
“Yes,” I look up from my phone to discover my
mom yelling at me. She seems to be searching for
an answer to something. “What?” I asked.
She asked, “Did you not hear what I just said?”
No, I didn’t. I didn’t hear anything she said. I
usually don’t hear a single word (A)[saying / said]
to me by anyone. And why is that? It’s because my
eyes are fixed on my phone. My mom always asks
me, “What is so interesting on your phone?” I
never know how to answer that because even I
don’t know what’s so interesting on my phone.
I have a bad case of anxiety ⓐ_____________________
_____________________________. I spend most of my day
on social media. I fear missing out on social media.
I fear not being in the know of (B)[that / what]
everyone is discussing. I fear not being in the know
of what my friends are posting on social media.
My mom thinks I’m addicted to my phone. Older
people think teenagers like me have an addiction
to their phones and computers. But I wouldn’t say
it’s an addiction to a device. It’s an addiction to
social media. It’s an addiction to being online, or in
other words, a fear of not being online.
Basically, I have severe FOMO, for (C)[what / which]
I’m in desperate need of a cure. Maybe this spring
break could be a chance to find one.

solution: (A) 앞의 명사구 a single word를 수식하는 분사로, 수식받는 명사구 a single word가 ‘말해진’ 대상이므로 수동 관계를 나 타내는 과거분사 said가 알맞다. (B) 뒤에 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(everyone is discussing)을 이끌어 전치사 of의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로, 선행사를 포함하여 ‘~하는 것’의 의미를 갖는 관계대 명사 what이 알맞다. (C) 주절에 콤마로 연결되어 있고, 뒤에 완전한 절(I‘m in desperate need of a cure)이 이어지고 있으므로, 접속사 역할 을 하면서 완전한 절을 이끌 수 있는 ’전치사+관계대명사‘의 형태가 되어야 한다. 이때 관계대명사 what은 완전한 절을 이 끌 수 없으므로, which가 알맞다.

Day 4
I woke up late in the morning and reached for my
phone. I swiped my phone open only to remember
my social media apps were no longer there. Old
habits die hard. After breakfast, (A)나는 인터넷에 접
속하고 싶은 강한 충동을 느꼈지만, 이에 굴복하고 싶
지는 않았다. So, I decided to go out for a walk.
While walking in the park, I probably glanced at
my phone 20 times. At one moment, I looked at
the people around me, most of whom had their
eyes glued to their phones. I moved my gaze upward
and noticed how purely blue the sky was, without a
single cloud in sight. All around the park, trees
slowly swayed back and forth. Soon I found myself
taking a couple of pictures of the peaceful scene.
After lunch, I took out my old guitar from under
my bed. At first, it was because I was bored, but I
ended up playing it all afternoon. It didn’t matter
that I’m not really good at it. It just felt great that
I was lost in doing something for several hours
without getting interrupted by my phone.

How long did the writer spend taking photos?
Why did the writer take out her old guitar?
Why did playing the guitar make the writer feelgood?

at a place where I didn’t belong, which was quickly
replaced by a sense of ⓐ_________. I really shouldn’t
have gone back to a social media site in the middle
of my detox.
Day 11
This was the first day my phone felt more like a
brick in my pocket than a digital device. I could
already feel (B)[bound by / free from] worrying
about posting something and hoping it would get
some likes. At a gathering with my friends, it was
fun to get asked over and over again about how I
was surviving without social media. Sam said, “I
don’t think I could give up social media for even
one day.” My immediate thought was: Then you
really need to give it up! I didn’t actually say that,
although I wanted to.
Day 14
Toward the end of the day, I reflected on my
social media break and what things had been like
before. I realized that social media had taken some
control of me. It’s kind of ⓑ____________ that all I
did was envy others for their perfectly happy
moments in life, dress up my everyday events, and
think up ways to get others to like my posts.
From now on, I want to be in control of how I
use something or do something, not the other way
around. Tomorrow, I will return to my social media
activities, but in more careful and controlled ways.
I’m going to stick to just a couple of sites that I
really need, while making absolutely sure that my
activities
are

/

with

Part 2 My Two-week Detox
Day 4
I woke up late in the morning and reached for my
phone. I swiped my phone open only to remember
my social media apps were no longer there.
_______________________________________. After breakfast,
I felt a strong urge to go online, to which I didn’t
want to give in. So, I decided to go out for a walk.
While walking in the park, I probably glanced at
my phone 20 times. At one moment, I looked at
the people around me, most of whom had their
eyes glued to their phones. I moved my gaze
upward and noticed how purely blue the sky was,
without a single cloud in sight. All around the park,
trees slowly swayed back and forth. Soon I found
myself taking a couple of pictures of the peaceful
scene.
After lunch, I took out my old guitar from under
my bed. At first, it was because I was bored, but I
ended up playing it all afternoon. It didn’t matter
that I’m not really good at it. It just felt great that
I was lost in doing something for several hours
without getting interrupted by my phone.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Old habits die hard.
Look before you leap.
Well begun, half done.
Out of sight, out of mind.
Do in Rome as the Romans do.

not enough, there have been contests to try to
memorize its endless sequence of digits that never
repeat. Devin Powell was once ⓑchallenged to a pi
digit memorizing contest.
(A) He sat down at the piano and started to play
with that, which allowed him to identify the
phrases that sounded really neat. He tried some
parts in a major key and some in a minor key,
playing with different arrangements of blocks
from pi. He ended up ⓒcalled it Lullapi.
(B) A few years before that, he had covered the
World Memory Championship as a reporter and
watched
someone
memorize
a
randomly
ordered deck of cards in less than 19 seconds.
Powell spent a lot of time talking to people
about how they pulled off these seemingly
impossible
demonstrations
of
memory.
He
learned ⓓwhat it was not really due to some
kind of natural talent for memorizing things,
but some skills of using associations.
(C) He tried to get to 50 digits. After careful
consideration, he decided to associate the
digits with music. He mapped the numbers to
the notes on the musical scale; the bigger the
number, ⓔthe high up on the scale it went. At
first, he was only going to have these tones in
his head so that he could memorize the digits,
but as he mapped the very first five digits, he
found that it sounded really nice, like a lullaby.

According to environmental conservationists, some
100 million sharks are killed every year, far
exceeding the average rebound rate for many shark
populations. This number has risen sharply ever
since the release of the 1975 movie Jaws, ⓐ[which
/ in which] an enormous great white shark terrorizes
a resort island off the coast of Massachusetts.
Sharks have ⓑ[demonized / been demonized] on
screen for decades, as in Finding Nemo, Sharknado,
47 Meters Down, and many others.
In addition to the development of an irrational
fear of sharks, it has been suggested that people
are less likely to support and donate money toward
conserving sharks than other marine animals or
even other predators, despite a strong need to
maintain a healthy shark population for a balanced
ecosystem. Why do we have such a hard time
helping sharks but don’t have similar problems
when it comes to ⓒ[help / helping] tigers? What
really influences our fear of sharks?

ⓒ

As if celebrating the number with a holiday were
not enough, there have been contests to try to
memorize its endless sequence of digits that never
repeat. Devin Powell was once challenged to a pi
digit memorizing contest. A few years before that,
he had covered the World Memory Championship
as a reporter and watched someone memorize a
randomly ordered deck of cards in less than 19
seconds. ⓐPowell은 이런 겉보기에 불가능한 기억력
시연을 그들이 어떻게 해냈는지에 관해 많은 시간을
사람들과 이야기하며 보냈다. He learned that it was
not really due to some kind of natural talent for
memorizing
things,
but
some
skills
of
using
associations.
He tried to get to 50 digits. After careful
consideration, he decided to ⓑ________________________
______________________________. He mapped the numbers
to the notes on the musical scale; the bigger the
number, the higher up on the scale it went. At first,
he was only going to have these tones in his head
so that he could memorize the digits, but as he
mapped the very first five digits, he found that it
sounded really nice, like a lullaby.
He sat down at the piano and started to play with
that, which allowed him to identify the phrases that
sounded really neat. He tried some parts in a major
key and some in a minor key, playing with different
arrangements of blocks from pi. He ended up
calling it Lullapi.

choices: rely on his natural memorization talent
arrange the digits in alphabetical orders
replace the numbers with random symbols
link the digits to meaningful repetitions of words
create musical associations to help memorize thedigits

In a series of experiments, the researchers found
that music indeed has the power to influence public
opinions about sharks. ⓐTo measure the effect of
scary music in shark documentaries, the researchers
(A)[excluded / recruited] 2,181 participants to watch
a clip from a documentary, which featured sharks
ⓑswimming around harmlessly, not eating anything.
Some participants watched the clip with the music
that originally accompanied the shark scenes in the
documentary, a track called Sharks, which was
considered ominous by an independent music
expert. Other participants watched the same clip
ⓒaccompanying by (B)[creepy / upbeat] background
music. A third set of participants watched the clip
with no music at all. After watching the clips, all
the participants ⓓwere asked to describe their
attitudes toward sharks. The results showed that
participants who viewed the video with its original
ominous music ⓔreporting more negative attitudes
toward sharks than those who viewed the same
scenes set to cheery music or silence. Moreover,
they determined that these negative attitudes were
not simply due to the music alone, but rather the
(C)[combination / separation] of the video and
audio. In a separate set of experiments, the subjects
were asked to either listen to scary or cheery
music, or sit in silence, without watching anything.
It turned out ⓕthat there was no effect on the
attitudes toward sharks among these subjects.

(B) 첫 번째 집단은 불길하다고 여겨지는 음악이 있는 장면을 보도록 했고, 세 번째 집단은 아무런 음악 없이 영상을 시청하 도록 했다고 했으며, 불길한 원곡과 함께 영상을 시청한 참가 자들을 쾌활한 음악이나 정적 속에서 본 참가자들과 비교하는 실험 결과가 뒤에 이어지므로, 두 번째 집단인 또 다른 참가자 들은 동일한 영상을 긍정적인 분위기의 배경 음악과 함께 시 청했다는 흐름으로 upbeat(낙관적인)가 알맞다. As if celebrating the number with a holiday were
not enough, there have been contests to try to
memorize (A)[its / their] endless sequence of digits
that never repeat. Devin Powell was once challenged
to a pi digit memorizing contest. A few years
before that, he had ⓐcovered the World Memory
Championship as a reporter and watched someone
(B)[memorize / to memorize] a randomly ordered
ⓑdeck of cards in less than 19 seconds. Powell spent
a lot of time talking to people about how they
ⓒpulled off these seemingly impossible demonstrations
of memory. He learned that it was not really due
to some kind of natural talent for memorizing
things, but some skills of using associations.
He tried to get to 50 digits. After careful
consideration, he decided to associate the digits
with music. He mapped the numbers to the notes
on the musical ⓓscale; the bigger the number, the
(C)[high / higher] up on the scale it went. At first,
he was only going to have these tones in his head
so that he could memorize the digits, but as he
mapped the very first five digits, he found that it
sounded really nice, like a lullaby.
He sat down at the piano and started to play with
that, which allowed him to identify the phrases that
sounded really (D)[neat / neatly]. He tried some
parts in a major ⓔkey and some in a minor key,
playing with different arrangements of blocks from
pi. He ended up calling it Lullapi.

In a series of experiments, the researchers found
that music indeed has the power to influence public
opinions about sharks. ⓐ상어 다큐멘터리 속 무서운
음악의 효과를 측정하기 위해, 연구자들은 아무것도
먹지 않고 무해하게 헤엄치는 상어의 모습이 나오는
다큐멘터리 한 편의 영상을 시청하도록 2,181명의 참
가자들을 모집했다. Some participants watched the
clip with the music that originally accompanied the
shark scenes in the documentary, a track called
Sharks, which was considered (A)[eerie / lively] by
an independent music expert. Other participants
watched the same clip accompanied by cheery
background music. A third set of participants watched
the clip with no music at all. After watching the
clips, all the participants were asked to describe
their attitudes toward sharks. The (B)[predictions /
results] showed that participants who viewed the
video with its original ominous music reported more
negative attitudes toward sharks than those who
viewed the same scenes set to cheery music or
silence.
Moreover,
they determined
that
these
negative attitudes were not simply due to the music
alone, but rather the combination of the video and
audio. In a separate set of experiments, the subjects
were asked to either listen to scary or cheery
music, or sit in silence, without watching anything.
It turned out that there was a (C)[negligible /
significant] effect on the attitudes toward sharks
among these subjects.

livelypredictionssignificant

(B) 영상을 본 후 모든 참가자들이 상어에 대한 자신의 태도를 기술하도록 요청받은 이후의 과정으로, 불길한 원곡과 함께 영 상을 시청한 참가자들이 상어에 대해 더 부정적인 태도를 나 타냈다는 결과가 뒤에 이어지므로, 실험 결과를 언급하는 흐름 이 되는 results(결과)가 알맞다. (C) 상어에 대한 부정적인 태도가 단순히 음악 때문만이 아니 라 오히려 영상과 음향의 조합에 기인한 것임을 밝혀냈다고 했으므로, 관련된 별도의 실험에서 아무것도 보지 않고 무서운 음악이나 쾌활한 음악을 듣거나 정적 속에 앉아 있도록 요청 받은 경우 피실험자의 태도에 영향이 미미했다는 흐름이 되는 negligible((영향 등이) 무시할 수 있는 정도의, 대수롭지 않은) 이 알맞다.

The study also looked at how public attitudes
toward sharks can affect efforts to save them. “By
highlighting that ominous background music is
associated with negative attitudes toward sharks, we
hope to start a conversation about ways we can
ⓐenhance public perception of these ecologically
important animals,” says Andrew P. Nosal, an
associate professor of biology at Point Loma
Nazarene University.
Elizabeth Keenan, an assistant professor in the
Marketing unit of Harvard Business School, says that
ⓑunfavorable public opinions about sharks continue
to harm conservation efforts, which they are in
desperate need of. “Any organization that intends
to ⓒpositively promote sharks or any other creature
should carefully consider the soundtracks they
choose,” says Keenan. “While it may be tempting to
include
ominous
soundtracks
for
entertainment
value, for instance, our research shows there is a
potential ⓓrisk in doing so.”
While this study focuses on sharks, the findings
provide a general lesson about the marketing
power of background music, which may well take a
front seat toward influencing consumer choices.
“ⓔCognitive factors such as background music are
known
to
affect
consumers’ preferences,”
says
Keenan. “The key lies in determining whether these
factors are influencing consumers in ways that are
in line with companies’ intended outcomes.”

solution: ⓑ ‘consider+목적어+(to be+)보어(~을 …인 것으로 여기다)‘ 구문의 수동 표현인 ’be considered+(to be+)보어(~가 …인 것 으로 여겨지다)‘를 이루어야 하므로 형용사 ominous가 알맞다. 참고로, 부사는 보어 자리에 올 수 없다. ⓒ than 뒤에 비교 대상으로 이어진 대명사 those를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루는 주격 관계대명사 자리이며, those가 흐름상 participants(참가자들)를 가리키므로, 사람 선행사와 쓰이는 관 계대명사 who가 알맞다. ⓓ 주어 the subjects(피실험자들)가 ’요청받은‘ 대상이며 뒤에 목적어 없이 ’ask+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)(~에게 …하도 록 요청하다)‘의 to부정사가 바로 이어지고 있으므로, 수동 표 현인 ’be asked+to부정사(…하도록 요청받다)‘를 이루는 과거시 제 수동태 were asked가 알맞다.

body:
In a series of experiments, the researchers found
that music indeed has the power to influence public
opinions about sharks. To measure the effect of
scary music in shark documentaries, the researchers
recruited 2,181 participants to watch a clip from a
documentary,
which
featured
sharks
swimming
around
harmlessly,
not eating
anything.
Some
participants watched the clip with the music that
originally accompanied the shark scenes in the
documentary, a track called Sharks, which was
considered ominous by an independent music
expert. Other participants watched the same clip
accompanied by cheery background music. A third
set of participants watched the clip with no music
at all. After watching the clips, all the participants
were asked to describe their attitudes toward
sharks. The results showed that participants who
viewed the video with its original ominous music
reported more negative attitudes toward sharks than
those who viewed the same scenes set to cheery
music or silence. Moreover, they determined that
these negative attitudes were not simply due to the
music alone, but rather the combination of the
video and audio. In a separate set of experiments,
the subjects were asked to either listen to scary or
cheery music, or sit in silence, without watching
anything. It turned out that there was no effect on
the attitudes toward sharks among these subjects.

the positive and negative impact of scary musicon shark behavior
the role of audiovisual combinations in lesseningviewers’ fear of sharks
why watching documentaries without musicenhances concentration
experimental research on how documentarymusic affects impressions of sharks

The study also looked at how public attitudes
toward sharks can affect efforts to save them. “By
highlighting that ominous background music is
associated with negative attitudes toward sharks, we
hope to start a conversation about ways we can
improve public perception of these ecologically
important animals,” says Andrew P. Nosal, an
associate professor of biology at Point Loma
Nazarene University.
Elizabeth Keenan, an assistant professor in the
Marketing unit of Harvard Business School, says that
negative public opinions about sharks continue to
harm conservation efforts, which they are in desperate
need of. “Any organization that intends to positively
promote sharks or any other creature should carefully
consider the soundtracks they choose,” says Keenan.

Part 1 FOMO (Fear of Missing Out)
“Selena. SELENA!”
“Yes,” I look up from my phone to discover my
mom ⓐyelling at me. She seems to be searching
for an answer to something. “What?” I asked.
She asked, “Did you not hear what I just said?”
No, I didn’t. I didn’t hear anything she said. I
usually don’t hear a single word said to me by
anyone. And why is that? It’s because my eyes are
fixed on my phone. My mom always asks me,
“What is so interesting on your phone?” I never
know how ⓑto answer that because even I don’t
know what’s so interesting on my phone.
I have a bad case of anxiety ⓒthat comes from
not checking my phone. I spend most of my day
on social media. I fear missing out on social media.
I fear not being in the know of what everyone is
discussing. I fear not being in the know of what my
friends are posting on social media.
My mom thinks I’m addicted to my phone. Older
people think teenagers like me have an addiction
to their phones and computers. But I wouldn’t say
it’s an addiction to (A)___________. It’s an addiction
to (B)___________. It’s an addiction to ⓓbeing online,
or in other words, a fear of not being online.
Basically, I have severe FOMO, ⓔwhich I’m in
desperate need of a cure. Maybe this spring break
could be a chance to find one.

Volunteering has a great deal of benefits. (A) Not
only ⓐ[you / do you] make a positive impact on
someone’s life, but you gain valuable skills for your
career. (B) It even reduces stress and anxiety. (C)
With busy schedules, it can be hard to find the
time to commit to volunteer work. (D) Here are a
few ways to virtually volunteer. (E)
First, you could be a part of the effort to lend
support
to
senior
citizens
who
struggle
with
loneliness. Typically, volunteer “phone friends” make
regular calls to chat and check in with these
people. Second, you can help people with low or
no vision with their everyday tasks. Through a live
video call, you can offer visual assistance to those
who need it with tasks such as reading “use by”
dates and instructions on food packages, ⓑ[that /
which] helps them to lead more independent lives.
Finally, if you have an interest in wildlife and its
conservation, you can help with animal monitoring
work by watching live videos of animal habitats
around the world. Monitoring these animals ⓒ[help
/ helps] protect wildlife and develop methods of
conserving them.
Helping others and giving back to the community
can be very rewarding. It can make your day more
meaningful and productive. It is also a great way to
connect with new people and cultures. For those
who believe in karma, if you do good things for
others, good things will happen to you!

Day 11
This was the first day my phone felt more like a
brick in my pocket ⓓthan a digital device. I could
already feel free from worrying about posting
something and hoping it would get some likes. At
a gathering with my friends, it was fun to get
asked over and over again about how I was
surviving without social media. Sam said, “I don’t
think I could give up social media for even one
day.” My immediate thought was: Then you really
need to ⓔgive up it! I didn’t actually say that,
although I wanted to.
Day 14
Toward the end of the day, I reflected on my social
media break and what things had been like before. I
realized that social media had taken some control of
me. ㉡내가 한 것이라곤 다른 사람들의 완벽하게 행복
한 삶의 순간들 때문에 그들을 시기하고, 내 일상을 그

From now on, I want to be in control of how I
use something or do something, not the other way
around. Tomorrow, I will return to my social media
activities, but in more careful and controlled ways.
I’m going to stick to just a couple of sites that I

다음 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?

In a series of experiments, the researchers found
that music indeed has the power to influence public
opinions about sharks. To measure the effect of
scary music in shark documentaries, the researchers
recruited 2,181 participants to watch a clip from a
documentary,
which
featured
sharks
swimming
around harmlessly, not eating anything.
(A) After watching the clips, all the participants were
asked to describe their attitudes toward sharks.
The results showed that participants who viewed
the video with its original ominous music
reported more negative attitudes toward sharks
than those who viewed the same scenes set to
cheery music or silence.
(B) Moreover, they determined that these negative
attitudes were not simply due to the music alone,
but rather the combination of the video and audio.
In a separate set of experiments, the subjects
were asked to either listen to scary or cheery
music, or sit in silence, without watching anything.
It turned out that there was no effect on the
attitudes toward sharks among these subjects.
(C) Some participants watched the clip with the
music that originally accompanied the shark
scenes in the documentary, a track called
Sharks, which was considered ominous by an
independent music expert. Other participants
watched the same clip accompanied by cheery
background music. A third set of participants
watched the clip with no music at all.
solution: 음악이 실제로 상어에 대한 여론에 영향력이 있다는 것을 밝 혀낸 연구자들이 상어 다큐멘터리 속 무서운 음악의 효과를 측정하기 위해 아무것도 먹지 않고 무해하게 헤엄치는 상어의 모습이 나오는 영상을 시청할 참가자들을 모집했다는 주어진 글 다음에, 참가자들 중 일부는 상어 장면을 불길하다고 여겨 진 ‘Sharks’라는 음악과 함께, 또 다른 참가자들은 동일한 영상 을 쾌활한 배경 음악과 함께, 세 번째 집단은 영상을 아무런 음악 없이 각각 시청했다는 내용의 (C), 영상을 본 후 참가자 들은 상어에 대한 자신의 태도를 기술해 달라고 요청받았고 그 결과 불길한 원곡과 함께 영상을 시청한 참가자들이 다른 두 집단에 비해 상어에 대해 더 부정적인 태도를 나타냈다는 내용의 (A), Moreover(이에 더해)로 시작하여 또 다른 실험 결 과로서 부정적인 태도가 단순히 음악 때문만이 아니라, 오히려 영상과 음향의 조합에 기인했다는 것을 보여 주었다는 내용을 언급하며, 별도의 실험에서 아무것도 보지 않고 무서운 음악이 나 쾌활한 음악을 듣거나 정적 속에 앉아 있도록 요청받았던 피실험자들의 경우 상어에 대한 태도에 아무런 영향이 없었다 고 구체적으로 설명하는 (B)로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다.
